content.title: Fernandez's marathon win, Kostyuk's retirement headline Day 3 in Ningbo
content.description: Leylah Fernandez outlasted Aliaksandra Sasnovich in a 3-hour, 3-minute battle Wednesday to reach the Ningbo quarterfinals, while Marta Kostyuk's retirement propelled Ekaterina Alexandrova into the last eight and clinched Karolina Muchova's spot at the WTA Finals Indian Wells bid.

related.label: Meet your elite eight: A snapshot of the 2026 WTA Finals field
Karolina Muchova secures final qualification place for FAGE WTA Finals Indian Wells
Swiatek withdraws from Ningbo, ends season to 'rest and recover'

content.body:
Leylah Fernandez came from 5-3 down in the opening set before surviving a 3-hour, 3-minute shot-making duel to defeat qualifier Aliaksandra Sasnovich 7-5, 6-7 (3), 6-3 in the BNB Ningbo Open second round Wednesday.

Ningbo: Scores | Order of play | Draws

The result sends the Canadian to her fifth WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz quarterfinal of 2026 and her first in Ningbo. She improved to 3-2 overall against Sasnovich, including 3-0 on hard courts. Despite the challenges Sasnovich presented, Fernandez said staying positive and composed was the key to advancing.

"Just enjoying the battle," Fernandez said in her on-court interview. "It was so tough, but it was also so much fun playing in front of a wonderful crowd in a great stadium. So I'm just happy I was able to stay positive and calm in those moments. But I just hope it doesn't happen again and I get to keep my focus up for the whole match."

Kostyuk's retirement sends Alexandrova to quarters, Muchova to WTA Finals

Fernandez's next opportunity to do that will come against Ekaterina Alexandrova, last year's runner-up, who advanced to her second straight Ningbo quarterfinal when No. 3 seed Marta Kostyuk retired after dropping the first set 6-4 of their second-round match Wednesday.

The ramifications extend beyond Ningbo. With Kostyuk no longer able to claim the title, Karolina Muchova has secured the final berth at the WTA Finals Indian Wells. The 30-year-old will make her first appearance at the year-end championships.

Locked in for FAGE WTA Finals Indian Wells 💪 Karolina Muchova confirms her place on #TheUltimateStage, completing the 2026 singles line-up! Get your tickets to see the season's top 8 players take to the court! https://t.co/da5lfZ1CWV @FAGEUSA | #WTAFinals https://t.co/ENuqZHSDUo

— wta (@WTA) October 21, 2026

For Alexandrova, the retirement creates opportunities on multiple fronts. She remains in contention for a title that slipped away last year after she won the opening set against Elena Rybakina in the final before capturing just two games across the final two sets.

It also sets up a rematch with Fernandez, who defeated Alexandrova in three sets last week in Wuhan. Alexandrova enters the matchup having spent significantly less time on court in Ningbo, needing just 1 hour, 53 minutes to reach the quarterfinals compared with Fernandez's 5 hours, 52 minutes.

Another marathon would not be surprising, as their last three meetings have all gone the distance. Alexandrova owns a 3-2 edge in the head-to-head.

Bucsa, Melichar-Martinez overcome difficult draw to advance

One of the biggest perks of earning the No. 1 seed is a more favorable draw, particularly early in a tournament. That was not the case for Cristina Bucsa and Nicole Melichar-Martinez, who opened their Ningbo campaign against doubles standouts Sara Errani and Jasmine Paolini.

Bucsa and Melichar-Martinez embraced the challenge, defeating Errani and Paolini 7-5, 6-3 in 1 hour, 32 minutes Wednesday to reach the quarterfinals and extend their strong season. The top seeds were clutch when it mattered most, breaking serve in the final game of both sets.

The Guadalajara champions and Rome runners-up have already sewn up a spot in the WTA Finals Indian Wells, while Errani and Paolini maintain a tentative hold on the eighth and final qualifying position.

content.title: Karolina Muchova secures final qualification place for FAGE WTA Finals Indian Wells
content.description: The elite eight singles field is set after Karolina Muchova secured the final place, earning a second WTA Finals qualification after winning titles in Doha and Bad Homburg and reaching the Wimbledon final.

related.label: How Jessica Pegula’s discipline earned her another trip to the WTA Finals
Three teams secure places in the WTA Finals Indian Wells doubles field
FAGE named title partner of WTA Finals through 2029

content.body:
• Karolina Muchova is the eighth and final singles qualifier for the WTA's season-ending championships
  • Muchova won two titles in 2026 at Doha and Bad Homburg and overall reached four finals
  • Two additional doubles teams also confirmed their participation: Hsieh Su-Wei & Jelena Ostapenko and Ellen Perez & Demi Schuurs

Get your tickets here for this year's WTA Finals at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden

The WTA on Wednesday announced Karolina Muchova has qualified for the FAGE WTA Finals Indian Wells to confirm the star-studded singles field and set tennis' ultimate stage for the world's best athletes.

Muchova is the eighth and final singles qualifier for the preeminent championships in women's sport, joining PIF WTA World No.1 Elena Rybakina, Indian Wells and Miami champion Aryna Sabalenka, Roland-Garros winner Mirra Andreeva, Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova, American superstars Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula along with trailblazing mother Elina Svitolina at Indian Wells.

"Earning a place at the FAGE WTA Finals is an extraordinary achievement, and I can't wait to welcome our eight singles players to Indian Wells," WTA Finals Tournament Director Garbiñe Muguruza said. "This is the ultimate stage, where the best play the best. With its passionate fans and stunning desert backdrop, the Indian Wells Tennis Garden will be a fantastic setting to crown our champions."

Muchova, who is from the Czech Republic, has qualified for the WTA Finals for the second time after withdrawing from the 2023 event because of an injury.

The doubles teams of Hsieh Su-Wei & Jelena Ostapenko and Ellen Perez & Demi Schuurs also confirmed their qualification for the FAGE WTA Finals Indian Wells following impressive seasons on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz.

Karolina Muchova has enjoyed success this year at every level of the WTA Tour and across all three surfaces, winning titles on hard court at the WTA 1000 Qatar TotalEnergies Open (Doha) and on grass at the WTA 500 Bad Homburg Open powered by Solarwatt.

She reached an additional final on clay, finishing runner-up at the WTA 500 Porsche Tennis Grand Prix and also contested her second Grand Slam final at The Championships, Wimbledon.

Hsieh Su-Wei and Jelena Ostapenko will be making their second appearance as a team at the WTA Finals and enjoyed a run to the semifinals last year. Overall this will be Hsieh Su-Wei's seventh appearance, winning the title in 2013 and also finishing as runner-up three times, while this will be Ostapenko's fourth outing, having also qualified once for the WTA Finals in singles in 2017.

The pairing have reached two finals this year, kicking off 2026 by winning the WTA 500 Brisbane International and contesting the title match at the WTA 1000 Qatar TotalEnergies Open in Doha.

This season marks Ellen Perez and Demi Schuurs' first qualification as a team though both bring extensive WTA Finals experience, with Schuurs having reached three semifinals and Perez reaching the title match in 2023.

The duo have shown great consistency this season, contesting the final at the WTA 500 Bad Homburg Open powered by Solarwatt, reaching two semifinals at the Adelaide International and Porsche Tennis Grand Prix in Stuttgart (both WTA 500 events) and a further eight quarterfinals across 2026.

Hsieh Su-Wei & Ostapenko and Perez & Schuurs' qualification leaves one final doubles place remaining.

The WTA Finals Indian Wells features the Top 8 singles and doubles teams on the PIF Race to the WTA Finals Leaderboard (with the 8th spot going to the singles player and doubles team that have won a Grand Slam if ranked No.8 to No.20). This showcases the world’s best singles players and doubles teams competing in a round-robin format with the singles champion lifting the WTA Finals Billie Jean King Trophy and the doubles champions earning the WTA Finals Martina Navratilova Trophy. The prestigious season-ending tournament celebrates the best of the WTA on and off the court, delivering an unrivalled fan experience that blends sport, entertainment, and culture.

Get your tickets here for this year's WTA Finals at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden, one of the sport's premier destinations and tournament locations.

content.title: Vote: Which was your favorite WTA 1000 title run of 2026?
content.description: The 2026 WTA 1000 season is in the books, with nine players crowned champions across 10 tournaments. Vote for your favorite title run here.

related.label: Chwalinska’s breakout season reaches new heights with a WTA 1000 title in Wuhan
How Kostyuk shed the 'curse' of early expectations to win first WTA 1000 crown
How craft and consistency fueled Karolina Muchova’s dominant week in Doha

content.body:
The 2026 WTA 1000 season is in the books, with nine players crowned champions across 10 tournaments.

Four of those lifted a WTA 1000 trophy for the first time; five added to existing hauls at this level. From injury comebacks to surges in form, from home-soil glory to historic feats, each title run marked a riveting chapter in the WTA's year. But which was your favorite? Rewind through the champions' best points, then have your say below.

1. Karolina Muchova, Doha

R1: d. Jaqueline Cristian 6-2, 6-3
R2: d. [Q] Tereza Valentova 6-1, 6-4
R3: d. Karolina Pliskova 5-2, ret.
QF: d. Anna Kalinskaya 6-3, 6-4
SF: d. Maria Sakkari 3-6, 6-4, 6-1
F: d. [10] Victoria Mboko 6-4, 7-5

No. 14 seed Muchova snapped a title drought stretching back over six years to lift her second career trophy (following Seoul 2019), and the first at WTA 1000 level, at the Qatar TotalEnergies Open. It foreshadowed a career-best season for the Czech that's also included a second Grand Slam final appearance at Wimbledon and a third title in Bad Homburg. Muchova's defeat of Victoria Mboko in the final was the third of six Top 10 wins she has scored so far in 2026 -- her highest number in a single season.

2. Jessica Pegula, Dubai

R1: bye
R2: d. [Q] Varvara Gracheva 6-4, 6-0
R3: d. [16] Iva Jovic 6-4, 6-2
QF: d. [12] Clara Tauson 6-3, 2-6, 6-4
SF: d. [2] Amanda Anisimova 1-6, 6-4, 6-3
F: d. [7] Elina Svitolina 6-2, 6-4

No. 4 seed Pegula won her fourth career WTA 1000 tournament at the Dubai Duty Free Tennis Championships, and her 10th title overall. The American claimed two of her seven Top 10 wins of 2026 so far en route to the trophy, including a comeback from 6-1, 2-0 down in the semifinals against Amanda Anisimova.

3. Aryna Sabalenka, Indian Wells

R1: bye
R2: d. [Q] Himeno Sakatsume 6-4, 6-2
R3: d. Jaqueline Cristian 6-4, 6-1
R4: d. [16] Naomi Osaka 6-2, 6-4
QF: d. [10] Victoria Mboko 7-6(0), 6-4
SF: d. [14] Linda Noskova 6-3, 6-4
F: d. [3] Elena Rybakina 3-6, 6-3, 7-6(6)

After two previous losses in the BNP Paribas Open final in 2023 and 2025, No. 1 seed Sabalenka claimed her first Indian Wells title after saving one championship point in the final against Elena Rybakina -- avenging her loss to the Kazakhstani player in the Australian Open final. Sabalenka scored two of her seven Top 10 wins of 2026 so far en route to the trophy.

4. Aryna Sabalenka, Miami

R1: bye
R2: d. Ann Li 7-6(5), 6-4
R3: d. Caty McNally 6-4, 6-2
R4: d. [23] Zheng Qinwen 6-3, 6-4
QF: d. Hailey Baptiste 6-4, 6-4
SF: d. [3] Elena Rybakina 6-4, 6-3
F: d. [4] Coco Gauff 6-2, 4-6, 6-3

No. 1 seed Sabalenka became the fifth woman in the Open Era to successfully complete the Sunshine Double after following her Indian Wells title by defending her Miami Open crown. She notched another pair of Top 10 wins along the way, and the two consecutive trophies spearheaded her third career-best 15-match winning streak.

5. Marta Kostyuk, Madrid

R1: bye
R2: d. Yulia Putintseva 6-1, 6-3
R3: d. [5] Jessica Pegula 6-1, 6-4
R4: d. Caty McNally 6-2, 6-3
QF: d. [13] Linda Noskova 7-6(1), 6-0
SF: d. [LL] Anastasia Potapova 6-2, 1-6, 6-1
F: d. [9] Mirra Andreeva 6-3, 7-5

No. 26 seed Kostyuk compiled a 17-match clay-court winning streak, the longest at tour level this year, that included her first career WTA 1000 trophy at the Mutua Madrid Open. It also enabled the Ukrainian, who began the season at No. 26, to make her Top 10 debut in September. Kostyuk notched two of her eight Top 10 wins of 2026 so far in Madrid.

6. Elina Svitolina, Rome

R1: bye
R2: d. [Q] Noemi Basiletti 6-1, 6-3
R3: d. [32] Hailey Baptiste 6-1, 6-2
R4: d. [LL] Nikola Bartunkova 6-2, 6-3
QF: d. [2] Elena Rybakina 2-6, 6-4, 6-4
SF: d. [4] Iga Swiatek 6-4, 2-6, 6-2
F: d. [3] Coco Gauff 6-4, 6-7(3), 6-2

The Internazionali BNL d'Italia champion in 2017-18, No. 7 seed Svitolina reclaimed the Rome crown for a third time after an eight-year gap. The Ukrainian's battling run culminated in a trio of three-set victories over Top 5 opponents, including a 2-hour, 49-minute final defeat of Coco Gauff -- the longest WTA 1000 final of the season. Svitolina's fifth career WTA 1000 title was also her first since returning from maternity leave in 2023.

7. Iga Swiatek, Toronto

R1: bye
R2: d. Sara Bejlek 6-0, 6-3
R3: d. Viktorija Golubic 6-2, 6-1
R4: d. [10] Marta Kostyuk 3-6, 6-1, 6-2
QF: d. [15] Diana Shnaider 6-2, 6-1
SF: d. [9] Elina Svitolina 6-3, 1-6, 6-3
F: d. [2] Elena Rybakina 6-2, 6-3

No. 7 seed Swiatek snapped a 13-month title drought to lift her first National Bank Open trophy -- meaning that of the 15 biggest tournaments (four majors, 10 WTA 1000s and the WTA Finals) currently on the WTA calendar, the Pole is now only missing three: the Australian Open, Dubai and Wuhan. Swiatek's run included two of her four Top 10 wins of 2026.

8. Coco Gauff, Cincinnati

R1: bye
R2: d. Liudmila Samsonova 2-6, 6-4, 6-1
R3: d. [28] Ann Li 6-1, 7-6(3)
R4: d. [22] Marie Bouzkova 6-3, 6-2
QF: d. [10] Marta Kostyuk 6-2, 6-2
SF: d. Sara Bejlek 6-4, 6-1
F: d. [3] Jessica Pegula 6-2, 6-4

No. 4 seed Gauff claimed the Cincinnati Open crown for the second time (following her 2023 title), marking the first time that she has won a trophy at WTA 1000 level or above multiple times. Gauff's final defeat of Jessica Pegula was her fourth of five Top 10 victories so far this year, and marked the first all-American Cincinnati final since 1970.

9. Zheng Qinwen, Beijing

R1: d. [Q] Shi Han 7-6(6), 4-6, 6-2
R2: d. [15] Anna Kalinskaya 6-7(4), 6-4, 3-0 ret.
R3: d. [18] Marie Bouzkova 7-6(4), 4-6, 7-5
R4: d. Alina Charaeva 6-1, 2-6, 6-4
QF: d. [6] Elina Svitolina 6-3, 7-6(6)
SF: d. [13] Elise Mertens 7-5, 6-2
F: d. [4] Mirra Andreeva 7-5, 6-4

Ranked No. 54 but fresh off a run to the US Open quarterfinals as a qualifier, wild card Zheng became the China Open's first home champion with a battling run that included four three-setters and two Top 10 wins. It marked a spectacular return to form -- and to the Top 30 -- for Zheng, who underwent elbow surgery in July 2025 and whose ranking had slipped to No. 160 in June. She dropped 78 games en route to the title -- the second-most of any tour-level champion in the Open Era, only behind Madison Keys (who conceded 87 games on the way to the 2025 Australian Open title).

10. Maja Chwalinska, Wuhan

R1: d. Mayar Sherif 6-3, 6-2
R2: d. Marie Bouzkova 1-6, 6-1, 6-1
R3: d. [10] Iva Jovic 6-4, 6-1
QF: d. Maria Sakkari 6-0, 3-6, 7-5
SF: d. [7] Iga Swiatek 7-5, 6-1
F: d. Sonay Kartal 2-6, 6-4, 6-2

No. 16 seed Chwalinska's spectacular breakthrough season continued at the Dongfeng • Voyah Wuhan Open as the Pole became just the fourth player to win her maiden tour-level title at WTA 1000 level since the format's inception in 2009. Chwalinska, who started the year ranked No. 146 before becoming the first qualifier to reach the Roland Garros final in the Open Era, made her Top 20 debut following her Wuhan title run, which also included her first career Top 10 win -- over compatriot and childhood friend Iga Swiatek in the semifinals.

content.title: Swiatek withdraws from Ningbo, ends season to 'rest and recover'
content.description: Second seed Iga Swiatek has withdrawn from the BNB Ningbo Open because of a left thigh injury, and has announced that she's ending her season prematurely.

related.label: One WTA Finals singles spot remains open: Here’s how Karolina Muchova can clinch it
Chwalinska’s breakout season reaches new heights with a WTA 1000 title in Wuhan
Kerber wins the Luxembourg Ladies Tennis Masters for a second straight year

content.body:
Second-seeded Iga Swiatek has withdrawn from the BNB Ningbo Open because of a left thigh injury, and has opted to end her season early.

“I’ve been experiencing an ongoing problem with my left thigh over the past weeks," she said, "and I feel that giving myself the time to rest and recover is the right decision. I was really looking forward to competing here and I want to thank the tournament organizers and everyone who was hoping to see me play.

"I’m already looking forward to coming back next year!”

Swiatek was hampered by the same injury during her loss to Maja Chwalinska in the Wuhan semifinals last week.

Get well soon, Iga. ❤️ “After careful consideration, I’ve decided to withdraw from the tournament. I’ve been experiencing an ongoing problem with my left thigh over the past weeks and I feel that giving myself the time to rest and recover is the right decision…” https://t.co/x6xZJmEE36

— Ningbo Open (@wtaningboopen) October 20, 2026

Swiatek, who was still in contention for the last WTA Finals berth, later announced that she was calling it a season after what has been a challenging year. 

"This has been one of the most demanding seasons of my career, with a lot of challenges, changes and lessons along the way," she wrote on Instagram. "I’m especially proud of the work we’ve done in the second half of the year and the progress that came with it. It gives me a lot of confidence in what’s ahead."

"The past few months, or actually the past couple of years, have been incredibly intense, and I feel I need to rest and recover my body fully. So that’s exactly what I will do, a bit longer this time. 😉 I’ve decided to end my season here, which means I won’t be playing any more tournaments this year."

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Iga Świątek (@iga.swiatek)

Swiatek finishes the season with a 39-15 record and a title in Toronto.

The World No. 9 has been replaced in the draw by alternate Anastasia Zakharova.

content.title: Meet your elite eight: A snapshot of the 2026 WTA Finals field
content.description: It's official -- we have our eight-player WTA Finals singles field. Karolina Muchova qualified on Wednesday, and she will join Elena Rybakina, Aryna Sabalenka, Jessica Pegula, Coco Gauff, Mirra Andreeva, Linda Noskova and Elina Svitolina in Indian Wells.

related.label: Karolina Muchova secures final qualification place for FAGE WTA Finals Indian Wells
Swiatek withdraws from Ningbo, ends season to 'rest and recover'
Vote: Which was your favorite WTA 1000 title run of 2026?

content.body:
Karolina Muchova secured the last WTA Finals qualification berth on Wednesday, and with that we have our elite eight in the desert.

The WTA Finals at Indian Wells will feature three former champions, three newcomers and a wide-open field.

Ahead of the year-end tournament and culmination of the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz season, here's a snapshot of how they got to Indian Wells, and their outlook heading into the finale. 

Elena Rybakina

W-L record: 49-14

Titles won: 3 (Australian Open, Stuttgart, US Open)

Previous WTA Finals appearances: 3

Best WTA Finals result: 2025 champion

The skinny: Rybakina was the best player in the world this year. She burst out of the gate, following up her 2025 WTA Finals sweep with an Australian Open title, and ended the Grand Slam season with another major, at the US Open. She beat Aryna Sabalenka in both finals, and the latter win gave her the No. 1 ranking for the first time, ending Sabalenka's 99-week run at the top. She lost her opening match in Beijing and skipped Wuhan, but is playing this week in Ningbo, the last Finals qualifier still in action before Indian Wells.

READ MORE: A US Open champ and new No. 1, Rybakina completes trifecta with a ticket to WTA Finals

Aryna Sabalenka

W-L record: 47-10

Titles won: 3 (Brisbane, Indian Wells, Miami)

Previous WTA Finals appearances: 5

Best WTA Finals result: Finalist in 2022 and 2025

The skinny: On the surface, a season without a major title for the first time since 2022 might seem disappointing by Sabalenka’s standards. She still won 47 matches, made a pair of Grand Slam finals and won two WTA 1000 tournaments. Those back-to-back titles in Indian Wells and Miami were the high-water mark of her season, as she became just the fifth player in WTA Tour history to sweep the Sunshine Double. She's had her most success on hard courts, and has historically played very well at the Finals, a tournament she's eager to check off her bucket list. 

She enters the Finals with very little momentum, having lost two of three in Asia, but she should be well-rested.

READ MORE: One result at a time, Aryna Sabalenka keeps ending up at the WTA Finals

Mirra Andreeva

W-L record: 50-16

Titles won: 3 (Adelaide, Linz, Roland Garros)

Previous WTA Finals appearances: 0

The skinny: Andreeva has been prolific in 2026, tying Jessica Pegula for the most match-wins (50) on the WTA Tour. The apex of her season was at Roland Garros, where she won her first major. The 19-year-old made four other finals, winning two of them, and her hot hand has continued through the Asian Swing, where she's coming off a run to the final in Beijing. Currently at a career-high No. 3, Andreeva concludes the best season of her career fittingly, at her first WTA Finals. 

READ MORE: '150 percent of your focus': Andreeva on what it will take to compete at the WTA Finals

Jessica Pegula

W-L record: 50-13

Titles won: 2 (Dubai, Charleston)

Previous WTA Finals appearances: 4

Best WTA Finals result: 2023 final

The skinny: Pegula was a model of consistency once again in 2026. Tied with Andreeva for the most match-wins on tour, Pegula had the best winning percentage in the world and made five finals. Her two titles came earlier in the season, in Dubai and Charleston, and since April she's gone title-less, losing three consecutive finals in Berlin, Washington, DC and Cincinnati. Pegula has played just one match since the US Open, and should arrive at Indian Wells refreshed after some weeks off. 

READ MORE: How Jessica Pegula’s discipline earned her another trip to the WTA Finals

Coco Gauff

W-L record: 47-15

Titles won: 1 (Cincinnati)

Previous WTA Finals appearances: 4

Best WTA Finals result: 2024 champion

The skinny: Gauff's season kicked into gear in Miami, where she reached the final, and she made another WTA 1000 final in Rome a month and a half later. There was further heartbreak late in tournaments, with semifinal runs at Wimbledon and in Toronto, before she got her first title of the year in Cincinnati. She followed that up with a semifinal run in New York, in what was a highly productive Hard-Court Swing. Gauff is so dangerous on hard courts, and the 2024 champion will look to rebound after failing to get out of the group stage last year.

READ MORE: By the numbers: Gauff and Pegula are making WTA Finals history one year at a time

Elina Svitolina

W-L record: 46-14

Titles won: 2 (Auckland, Rome)

Previous WTA Finals appearances: 3

Best WTA Finals result: 2018 champion

The skinny: Svitolina returns to the Finals after seven years, and nearly a decade after she made her debut at the year-end tournament.  The 32-year-old won her first 10 matches of the season, including a title in Auckland and a semifinal run in Melbourne, and then won her biggest title of the year on clay, in Rome. She also reached the semis in Indian Wells, Stuttgart and Toronto, to go with a final in Dubai. Back-to-back quarterfinal runs in Beijing and Wuhan show that the 2018 champion is still in form at the tail end of the season. 

READ MORE: WTA Finals flashback: How Svitolina turned a shaky stretch in Asia into the biggest title of her career

Karolina Muchova

W-L record: 40-11

Titles won: 2 (Doha, Bad Homburg)

Previous WTA Finals appearances: 0

The skinny: It's hard to believe that when Muchova won the Qatar TotalEnergies Open in February, it was only her second career title, and first since 2019. It was the biggest title of her career, and it set the tone for the rest of the season, which included a second title in Bad Homburg and a runner-up finish at Wimbledon. That run to the final propelled her to a career-high No. 6 in the world. Muchova also made semifinals in Brisbane and Miami, and a final in Stuttgart. With her all-court game, athleticism and ability to hit any shot from any angle, she's one of the toughest outs in tennis.

READ MORE: Karolina Muchova secures final qualification place for FAGE WTA Finals Indian Wells

Linda Noskova

W-L record: 35-15

Titles won: 2 (Berlin, Wimbledon)

Previous WTA Finals appearances: 0

The skinny: Noskova's breakthrough came at Wimbledon, where she won her first career major as a No. 9 seed. Though the title was surprising, anyone who had been paying attention could see that she was a threat on grass, having beaten Pegula in the Berlin final a couple weeks earlier. But the 21-year-old proved that she can win on all surfaces in 2026, reaching the semis at Indian Wells earlier in the year and the quarterfinals of the US Open in September. Noskova withdrew from Wuhan with a left calf injury, but she should have enough time to recover for Indian Wells.

READ MORE: The first-timers who won the WTA Finals: Could Andreeva or Noskova be next?

content.title: FAGE named title partner of WTA Finals through 2029
content.description: FAGE will become title partner of the WTA Finals in 2026, with the agreement covering the championship’s move from Indian Wells to Charlotte and continuing through 2029.
content.body:
• Multi-year partnership begins at Indian Wells in 2026 and continues in Charlotte from 2027 to 2029

The WTA on Tuesday announced a multi-year partnership with international dairy company, FAGE, as title partner of the WTA Finals and Official Yogurt Partner of the WTA. In the latest step towards a new chapter for the season-ending championship, the partnership with FAGE will begin at Indian Wells, California in 2026 and continue into Charlotte, North Carolina, the WTA Finals’ new home, from 2027 to 2029.

FAGE is a heritage brand rooted in history and craftsmanship. Its commitment represents a significant endorsement of women’s tennis and the continued momentum of the WTA. As title sponsor of the WTA’s flagship event, FAGE will be integrated into the identity and experience of the WTA Finals, with brand visibility across broadcast and venue, product sampling, fan experiences and hospitality.

From 2027, the WTA and FAGE will work together to extend the opportunity beyond event week, creating further opportunities to engage fans and build visibility through year-round marketing and digital activity.

The partnership brings together FAGE’s commitment to promoting healthy, active lifestyles and the dedication to excellence embodied by the world’s top women tennis players. With nutrition playing an important role in supporting strength, endurance and recovery, FAGE’s support of the WTA Finals celebrates the connection between balanced nutrition, everyday well-being and elite performance, inspiring fans to pursue their own health and fitness goals on and beyond the court.

Valerie Camillo, WTA Chair, said: “Our ambition is to make the WTA Finals the Super Bowl of women’s sports—delighting fans, elevating the WTA Tour, and matching the world-class calibre of our athletes. FAGE’s commitment is a strong endorsement of the momentum behind this vision, women's tennis, and the opportunity ahead.”

Marina Storti, CEO of WTA Ventures, the commercial arm of the WTA, said: “We are thrilled to welcome FAGE, a globally recognised consumer brand with a strong commitment to promoting healthy, active lifestyles, as title partner of the WTA Finals. This multi-year partnership comes at an exciting time for the Finals and provides a long-term platform for us to grow together, elevate the event and celebrate the very best of women's tennis.”

Jeffrey Scipione, Chief Commercial Officer at FAGE, said: “Becoming title partner of the WTA Finals in Indian Wells and Charlotte marks an exciting next chapter in FAGE’s commitment to tennis. The WTA Finals celebrates the talent, dedication and exceptional achievements of the world’s best players, making it a natural fit for our brand that has stayed true to its roots and an uncompromising commitment to quality for 100 years.

“Both FAGE and the WTA are building on rich legacies while looking ahead to engaging with new generations of fans and consumers.”

FAGE’s partnership with the WTA builds on its existing portfolio in tennis, which also includes relationships with the US Open, LTA, ATP Finals and Davis Cup.

The partnership with FAGE advances the WTA’s ambition to establish the WTA Finals as the preeminent championship experience in women’s sport, providing an outstanding stage for the world’s best athletes, an exceptional experience for fans, and a compelling showcase for commercial partners. It also builds on the WTA’s commercial momentum in 2026, following the launch of long-term partnerships with Mercedes-Benz and Accenture.

The FAGE WTA Finals Indian Wells will take place from November 8 to November 15, 2026, bringing together the season’s top singles players and doubles teams to compete for one of the most prestigious titles in women’s tennis. From 2027, the season-ending showcase will move to Charlotte, where the FAGE WTA Finals Charlotte will begin its next chapter of establishing a defining moment on the global women’s sports calendar.

The partnership was brokered by the U.S. Rights Sales group at THE·TEAM, a leading global sports, music and entertainment company and WTA Ventures’ appointed Sales Agency of Record, in collaboration with SPORTFIVE the global sports marketing agency.

Tickets are available here for this year’s WTA Finals at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden.

content.title: Week in review: The moment of Maja's career and Kartal's improbable run
content.description: Maja Chwalinska won the first title of her career, Sonay Kartal came out of nowhere to reach a WTA 1000 final and more in the latest WTA week in review.

related.label: Vote: Which was your favorite WTA 1000 title run of 2026?
One WTA Finals singles spot remains open: Here’s how Karolina Muchova can clinch it
FAGE named title partner of WTA Finals through 2029

content.body:
And with that, the WTA 1000 season is in the books.

The final WTA 1000 tournament in Wuhan packed quite the punch, considering the shorter format, and produced one of the unlikeliest finals in recent memory. We had two first-time WTA 1000 finalists, fitting considering the season's remarkable parity, and a champion who put a bow on an improbable season.

There were also a large quantity of upsets and epic three-setters, and the WTA Finals field started to take greater shape.

Here's everything that went down on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz last week.

Star of the Week

Maja Chwalinska

When Chwalinska had her run to the Roland Garros final as a qualifier, it was one of the great stories in Grand Slam history, and surely one we'd never forget. But the question of whether it was a fluke was a valid one, considering the then-24-year-old came into the tournament ranked No. 114 in the world and had never reached a tour-level final, much less won a title.

Chwalinska proved in Wuhan that it was no fluke, and she is in fact the real deal, regardless of surface.

Chwalinska won the first WTA title of her career in Wuhan, picking up statement wins over Iva Jovic (her first Top 15 win) and countrywoman Iga Swiatek (her first Top 10 win) before coming from a set and a break down to beat Sonay Kartal in the final. 

The title propelled her 11 spots in the PIF WTA Rankings, to a career-high No. 11. She came into the season ranked No. 146 in the world.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by WTA (@wta)

Breakthrough of the Week

Sonay Kartal

Players often need ample time, and consistent match play, to return to form after an injury. Kartal apparently needs neither. In fact, in just her second tournament following a sixth-month stint on the sidelines with a back injury, Kartal produced the best week of her career. She doesn't have a title to show for it, but reached a WTA 1000 final for the first time. (She had never before been past the quarterfinals at a WTA 1000.)

Ranked No. 170 in the world coming into this tournament, she upset ninth-seeded Belinda Bencic, 15th-seeded Jasmine Paolini, fifth-seeded Elina Svitolina and former Grand Slam champion Jelena Ostapenko to get to the championship match. The end of the week will surely sting, as she was in prime position to close out the final, but she can take solace in the fact that she jumped 121 spots in the PIF WTA Rankings, to No. 49, and is now the No. 1 British player in the world.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by WTA (@wta)

Best Match of the Week

Ann Li d. Aryna Sabalenka, second round

What a sensational comeback for Li, who picked up the biggest win of her career against Sabalenka. Li came from a set and a break down in this one, and finally clinched the match on her 10th match point.

"I think on some of those match points I was about to lose my mind," Li said after the 3-6, 6-4, 7-6 (5) win. "I was about to crash out."

Biggest Upset of the Week

Shi Han d. Alexandra Eala, first round

So many to choose from, including the aforementioned Li-Sabalenka match. But we'll go with Shi's 4-6, 6-3, 6-3 win over 19th-seeded Eala. Shi, who came into the tournament ranked No. 217, had never beaten a player in the Top 100 at the start of the tournament. She did it three times last week, beating Peyton Stearns and Kamilla Rakhimova in qualifying before stunning Eala on home soil.

It was just the third main-draw win of her career, and first since 2024.

Best Comeback of the Week

Guo Hanyu d. Sorana Cirstea, first round

Chinese wild card Guo Hanyu managed to escape a bleak 6-1, 4-0 deficit against Cirstea, saving triple match point in the second-set tiebreak. The then-World No. 240 also trailed 5-3 in the third set before rallying to take the final four games for the 1-6, 7-6 (6), 7-5 win.

Best Shot of the Week

Karolina Muchova's leaping behind-the-back overhead

Another week, another absurd shot from Muchova, who manages to wow us in new and inventive ways every time she takes the court.

After Caty McNally brought her in with the drop shot, Muchova pushed the American into the corner with a running forehand. McNally hit a very solid backhand lob, but Muchova tracked it and ended the point, as only she can, with a leaping, twisting, behind-the-back overhead.

Best Stat of the Week

Swiatek makes WTA 1000 history

With her win over Ashlyn Krueger in the third round, Swiatek became the fastest player to reach the 150-win milestone at WTA 1000s, doing it in just her 187th WTA 1000 match.

Social Moment of the Week

Zheng stuns in Vogue

On the heels of her title in Beijing, Zheng Qinwen returned to the digital pages of Vogue. The spread did not disappoint, as per usual.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Zheng Qinwen (@zhengqinwen_tennis)

WTA Finals Updates of the Week

Pegula, Gauff, Svitolina clinch berths

Jessica Pegula and Coco Gauff qualified for the WTA Finals for the fifth consecutive time. Later in the week, Elina Svitolina joined them in the field, earning her first qualification berth since 2019.

One singles spot in the eight-player field remains. 

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by WTA (@wta)
content.author: Brad Kallet
content.summary: Maja Chwalinska won the first title of her career, Sonay Kartal came out of nowhere to reach a WTA 1000 final and more in the latest WTA week in review.

content.title: WTA icons celebrate Navratilova's 70th birthday at star-studded dinner
content.description: A host of WTA icons celebrated Martina Navratilova's 70th birthday in Miami on Sunday night, including Pam Shriver, Chris Evert, Rosie Casals, Mary Carillo, Arantxa Sanchez Vicario, Chanda Rubin and Gigi Fernandez.

related.label: Chwalinska’s breakout season reaches new heights with a WTA 1000 title in Wuhan
Life after Roland Garros: How Chwalinska embraced the tough moments and won in Wuhan
Three teams secure places in the WTA Finals Indian Wells doubles field

content.body:
Martina Navratilova celebrated her 70th birthday on Oct. 18, and she spent her special evening with a host of WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz legends.

The festivities took place at Casa Matilda in Miami, and the star-studded guests included Pam Shriver, Chris Evert, Rosie Casals, Mary Carillo, Arantxa Sanchez Vicario, Chanda Rubin and Gigi Fernandez.

Navratilova's wife, Julia Lemigova, was also present, as were their daughters, Emma and Victoria.

"Seventy is a big number," Navratilova said, "but I am grateful to have earned it. And no better way to celebrate than with my tennis nomadic champions, and of course my family and other friends. Having Chris there was the cherry on the cake."

It was quite the busy day for Navratilova, who flew from Santa Fe to Miami with Austin after both attended a charity fundraiser for First Serve - New Mexico.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Tracy Austin (@tracyaustin_)

"A very Happy birthday to a woman who has been in my life for 50 years now," Evert wrote on Instagram. "A great friend, an intense rival, and a wonderful human being. I wish you good health and happiness always.❤️(See you tonight!)."

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Chris Evert (@chrissieevert)

Carillo, who gave an all-time great Hall of Fame induction speech earlier this summer, showed off her brilliance and creativity again on this night, with a mockumentary that included tributes from Billie Jean King and Lindsay Davenport.

"To show Martina how adored she is, an utterly inaccurate and ridiculous mockumentary is clearly in order," Carillo said. "The result was a laughing love fest."

Evert also made a speech, as seen in the collection of photos that Shriver shared on Instagram.

"All time great night celebrating Martina’s 70th," Shriver wrote. "Grateful to tennis for offering up lifetime friendships. It’s now Monday in Miami and this celebration is my Mindset Monday post. I have celebrated and reflected a lot on this 12 day 5 city trip. I feel gratitude and love at bed time."

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Pam Shriver (@pamshriver_official)

"An incredible night celebrating Martina with so many friends! ✨️❤️" Rubin commented.

It's been a banner year for Navratilova, who took part in the International Tennis Hall of Fame festivities in Newport just before the US Open. Donning a Ted Tinling dress from her 1979 Wimbledon title run, she partnered with inductee Roger Federer in an exhibition match against Gabriela Sabatini and Marat Safin.

A couple months prior, Navratilova and Evert were the subjects of the critically acclaimed Netflix documentary "Chris & Martina: The Final Set", which chronicled their decades-long rivalry and respective battles with cancer.

Evert and Navratilova played an almost incomprehensible 80 times between 1973 and 1988, with the latter winning the back-and-forth head-to-head 43-37. Of the 80 matches, 60 came in finals and 14 came in Grand Slam finals. 

They both won 18 Grand Slam singles titles. Navratilova's nine Wimbledon titles are the most all-time, and Evert's seven French Open titles are the most all-time in the women's game.

content.title: Kerber wins the Luxembourg Ladies Tennis Masters for a second straight year
content.description: Angelique Kerber defeated Yanina Wickmayer in Sunday’s final, then reflected on the joy of returning to the court with a field of former Tour rivals, many of them mothers.
content.body:
For the second year in a row, former World No.1 Angelique Kerber was triumphant at the Luxembourg Ladies Tennis Masters, edging Belgium’s Yanina Wickmayer in Sunday’s title bout, 6-4, 6-2.

On her way to the title, Kerber also posted a quarterfinal win over Monica Puig -- who famously defeated the German in the gold medal match at the Rio Olympics -- and got the better of her good friend, former World No.2 Agnieszka Radwanska in the semis.

For her part, Wickmayer, making her first appearance at the event having retired in the summer of 2025, had advanced to the final by virtue of two match tiebreak nail-biters.  

In Friday’s opener, the former No.12 defeated Petra Kvitova -- back on court less than seven months after delivering her twin girls. On Saturday, she edged last year’s runner-up, Alizé Cornet, in the final four.

Rounding out the eight-woman field at the Coque arena this year was France’s Tatiana Golovin, who was dispatched by Radwanska in straight sets in the quarters and Slovakia’s Magdalena Rybarikova, who met a similar fate against Cornet.

“I don’t find the words right now to say how much fun I had on the court,” Wickmayer said in her runner-up speech.

“It was really great to be back and play all these amazing players and to see them again after a while. Most of us are moms now, so we’re living a different life, but it’s so nice to meet up on the court and give it our all and still find the joy in the fight.”

Kerber, the first player to win the event twice, received her trophy from Luxembourg prime minister Luc Frieden and expressed similar sentiments to the fans.

“Actually, I feel like I’m at home -- maybe I should move to Luxembourg!” she said, laughing. “This is such a great event, and to see the stands always full, it’s the most important thing for us. We feel the energy, we feel the competition that we had for 20 years playing on the Tour and we show the younger generations that moms can do it. It’s very special.”

For 25 years, Luxembourg hosted a popular stop on the WTA Tour, players embracing the family atmosphere at the event. The list of champions grew to include six former World No.1s, including Kim Clijsters, who captured the WTA 250 title a record five times.

By 2022, tournament director Danielle Maas and her team at International Women’s Tennis Promotion were keen to build on this legacy under a different format – and the current eight-woman, competitive prize money exhibition was conceived.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Luxembourg Ladies Tennis Masters (@luxladiestennismasters)

Appropriately enough, Clijsters reigned in the first edition held that year, defeating Martina Hingis in the final. In 2023, Kontaveit beat Andrea Petkovic for the crown and the 2024 final saw Flipkens conquer Martina Hingis.

Now established as a hot ticket not only for fans but also stars keen to maintain their atheticism into retirement, the Luxembourg Ladies Tennis Masters has evolved over its five stagings into a showcase of WTA role models and the principles espoused by Billie Jean King more than 50 years ago.

The invitational has developed its own traditions and once again, the nostalgic Jana Novotna Award was presented at a gala dinner before action got underway. This year’s recipient was Luxembourg’s own Anne Kremer, who won WTA titles at Auckland and Pattaya in 2000 and rose to World No.18 in 2002.

The award celebrates individuals who demonstrate special commitment to women’s tennis, in Luxembourg and abroad, just like the much-loved Czech champion did during her lifetime.

Kerber’s victory resulted in a winner’s check of €50,000 from a total purse of €110,000.

content.title: One WTA Finals singles spot remains open: Here’s how Karolina Muchova can clinch it
content.description: Karolina Muchova is sitting out Ningbo and Osaka, but she can secure the final place if Iga Swiatek and Marta Kostyuk fall short of key results in Ningbo.
content.body:
As the season enters its final stretch, one singles place remains up for grabs at the WTA Finals in Indian Wells. Seven players have qualified: Elena Rybakina, Aryna Sabalenka, Mirra Andreeva, Jessica Pegula, Coco Gauff, Elina Svitolina and Linda Noskova.

Three players remain in contention for the last spot: Karolina Muchova (No. 7, 4,735 points), Iga Swiatek (No. 9, 4,189) and Marta Kostyuk (No. 10, 3,920). Muchova is not playing this week, and Swiatek has withdrawn from Ningbo, leaving Kostyuk as the only player whose results can affect the race.

The scenario is straightforward: If Kostyuk does not reach the final, Muchova secures the last spot.

Kostyuk will open against Ekaterina Alexandrova on Wednesday. 

The WTA Finals begin Nov. 8 in Indian Wells.

content.title: Eala snaps losing streak in Ningbo to extend breakout 2026 season
content.description: Alexandra Eala defeated Diane Parry 6-3, 6-1 in Ningbo to secure her 34th tour-level victory of the 2026 season and advance to the second round of the WTA 500 event. The Filipino snapped a three-match losing streak with the win and will next meet No. 6 seed Diana Shnaider or qualifier Yulia Putinteseva.

related.label: Rankings Watch: Chwalinska makes Top 20 debut, Kartal vaults 121 places
Chwalinska’s breakout season reaches new heights with a WTA 1000 title in Wuhan
Kartal’s comeback gathers pace with landmark run to Wuhan final

content.body:
Before the 2026 season, the Philippines' Alexandra Eala had won just 15 tour-level matches in her career. On Monday, the 21-year-old recorded her 34th tour-level victory of the season, defeating France's Diane Parry in straight sets in the first round of the WTA 500 tournament in Ningbo, China.

Eala and Parry exchanged early breaks in the opening set. However, from 3-3, the Filipino won seven consecutive games to build a 6-3, 4-0 lead before closing out a 6-3, 6-1 victory in 1 hour, 17 minutes.

The win snapped a three-match losing streak for Eala, who had lost her opening matches in Singapore and Wuhan.

She gets it done ✅ Alexandra Eala defeats Parry 6-3, 6-1 and advances into the Round of 16 in Ningbo! #NingboOpen https://t.co/rmHWtzKFGH

— wta (@WTA) October 19, 2026

Eala was the more consistent player, hitting 12 winners while committing nine unforced errors for a winner-to-unforced-error ratio of 1.33. Parry, meanwhile, hit 11 winners and made 25 unforced errors, recording a ratio of 0.44.

"I'm very happy with my performance," Eala said in her postmatch interview. "I think it was a really good first round, tough first round.

"Diane is a great player and I think she's had a really good year. Congrats to her for the year she's done and really happy to be in the second round. I'm very happy to have won the first round."

As has been the case in nearly all her matches this year, the stadium was packed with Eala's supporters, a turnout she acknowledged in her interview.

"Thank you everyone. Thank you so much for the support. It really makes my job very fun, even in the difficult moments. I'm really happy to be here."

Eala will face either sixth-seeded Diana Shnaider or qualifier Yulia Putintseva in the second round. It would be her first meeting with either player.

The Filipino snapped a three-match losing streak with the win and will next meet No. 6 seed Diana Shnaider or qualifier Yulia Putinteseva.

content.title: Ashleigh Barty, Svetlana Kuznetsova on 2027 Hall of Fame ballot
content.description: Four-time Grand Slam champions Ashleigh Barty and Svetlana Kuznetsova have been announced as International Tennis Hall of Fame Class of 2027 nominees.

related.label: Eala snaps losing streak in Ningbo to extend breakout 2026 season
Rankings Watch: Chwalinska makes Top 20 debut, Kartal vaults 121 places
Chwalinska’s breakout season reaches new heights with a WTA 1000 title in Wuhan

content.body:
Ashleigh Barty and Svetlana Kuznetsova have been announced as nominees for the International Tennis Hall of Fame Class of 2027.

Barty is a 15-time WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz singles champion and 12-time doubles champion. That includes four Grand Slam titles, beginning with the 2018 US Open doubles title, alongside CoCo Vandeweghe. From there she won the 2019 French Open, Wimbledon in 2021 and the Australian Open in 2022.

The 30-year-old Australian also won the 2019 WTA Finals in Shenzhen.

Barty reached No. 1 in the PIF WTA Rankings earlier that summer, and spent 121 weeks at the top, including 114 consecutive weeks.

A two-time WTA Player of the Year (2019 and 2021), Barty retired in 2022 with a 305-102 singles record. This is her first year on the ballot.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by International Tennis Hall of Fame (@tennishallofame)

Kuznetsova, 41, is on the ballot for the second time. Kuznetsova won 18 WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz singles titles and 16 doubles titles during her 15-year career. That includes Grand Slam singles titles at the US Open in 2004 and Roland Garros in 2009. She also won a pair of Australian Open doubles titles, first with Alicia Molik in 2005 and then with Vera Zvonareva in 2012.

Kuznetsova, who reached career highs of No. 2 in singles and No. 3 in doubles, was also part of three Billie Jean King Cup championship teams.

"I am incredibly pleased that my achievements are still remembered and appreciated," Kuznetsova wrote on Instagram. "...To be in the Tennis Hall of Fame would be a great honor and joy for me!"

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Светлана Кузнецова 🎾✨ (@svetlanak27)

Also on the 2027 ballot is 2009 US Open champion Juan Martin del Potro, as well as four-time Paralympic gold medalist and 28-time major champion Shingo Kunieda, in the Wheelchair Tennis Category.

Fans can vote for their selections here, through Oct. 25. The top three vote-getters from the fan vote will have percentage points added to the results from the official voting group, which consists of journalists, tennis historians and Hall of Famers.

Nominees need at least 75 percent of the vote to get elected to the Hall of Fame.

The inductees will officially be announced later this fall.

content.title: Rankings Watch: Chwalinska makes Top 20 debut, Kartal vaults 121 places
content.description: Maja Chwalinska climbs to No. 11 after winning her first WTA title, while Sonay Kartal jumps 121 places to No. 49 after reaching the Wuhan final in her third tournament back.

related.label: Life after Roland Garros: How Chwalinska embraced the tough moments and won in Wuhan
Chwalinska’s breakout season reaches new heights with a WTA 1000 title in Wuhan
Former US Open champions Andreescu, Stephens climb rankings with titles

content.body:
The 2026 WTA 1000 season concluded last week with the 10th and final tournament at that level on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz, the Dongfeng • Voyah Wuhan Open.

Roland Garros finalist Maja Chwalinska continued her sensational breakthrough season by lifting her first WTA trophy, a title run that included her first career Top 10 win (over Polish compatriot Iga Swiatek in the semifinals) and culminated in a 2-6, 6-4, 6-2 final defeat of Sonay Kartal from a set and 2-0 down. The 2-hour, 43-minute final was the second-longest at WTA 1000 level this year, following Elina Svitolina's 2-hour, 49-minute triumph over Coco Gauff in Rome.

Chwalinska became the fourth player to win the first title of her career at WTA 1000 level since the format's inception in 2009, following Naomi Osaka (Indian Wells 2018), Bianca Andreescu (Indian Wells 2019) and Victoria Mboko (Montréal 2025). She also became just the third player since 1990 to reach her first two career finals at Grand Slam and/or WTA 1000/Tier I level, following Anna Kournikova (Key Biscayne 1998, Hilton Head 1999) and Amélie Mauresmo (Berlin 1998, Australian Open 1999).

Chwalinska, who turned 25 years old the day before the Wuhan tournament started, jumps 11 places from No. 22 to make her Top 20 debut at No. 11 -- having started 2026 ranked No. 146. She becomes the fourth Polish player in the Open Era to reach the Top 20, following Agnieszka Radwanska, Swiatek and Magda Linette.

Kartal also enjoyed a remarkable tournament in Wuhan. In March, the Briton had just scored her fifth career Top 20 win over Madison Keys in Indian Wells when a back injury forced her to retire against Elena Rybakina in the fourth road -- then sidelined her for the next six months. Ranked No. 56 at the time, Kartal only returned to action a month ago in the Billie Jean King Cup Finals; entering Wuhan, the third event of her comeback, her position had slipped to No. 170.

Kartal's run to the final included a sixth Top 20 win, over Belinda Bencic, followed by a second career Top 10 win against Elina Svitolina in the quarterfinals. Upsets of Jasmine Paolini and Jelena Ostapenko made it a quartet of victories over former Top 5 opponents, and made Kartal the lowest-ranked WTA 1000 or Tier I finalist in history (excluding the unranked Jennifer Capriati at Hilton Head 1990).

The 24-year-old's reward in the latest edition of the PIF WTA Rankings is a 121-place jump back into the Top 50 for the first time since February, landing at No. 49. Kartal is just five places behind the career high of No. 44 that she set in July 2025.

Ostapenko returns to Top 30; Li hits new career high

Wuhan's top two seeds were both felled in their opening second-round matches in three-set thrillers. Jelena Ostapenko saved three match points to oust Jessica Pegula, and a few hours later Ann Li closed out Aryna Sabalenka in a third-set tiebreak on her 10th match point.

Ostapenko went all the way to the semifinals, her second at WTA 1000 level in 2026, and the Latvian is bumped up 10 places this week from No. 34 to No. 24. Li, whose third career Top 10 win spearheaded a run to her first WTA 1000 quarterfinal, climbs six spots from No. 31 to a new career high of No. 25.

Pohankova, Guo boosted after strong showings as wild cards

Two players made stellar use of their Wuhan wild cards to reach the last 16 of a WTA 1000 event for the first time.

Seventeen-year-old Mia Pohankova, the 2025 Wimbledon junior champion, claimed a pair of Top 100 upsets over Anna Bondar and Wang Xiyu before falling to Maria Sakkari -- though despite that loss, Pohankova still has a winning 7-6 career record against Top 100 opposition. The Slovakian teenager soars 57 places from No. 202 to a new career high of No. 145 this week; she's now the fourth-highest ranked 2008-born player, behind Lilli Tagger (No. 57), Laura Samson (No. 116) and Emerson Jones (No. 134).

Reigning Wimbledon doubles champion Guo Hanyu has been making inroads into the singles tour over the past two years, qualifying for her first Grand Slam main draw at Roland Garros in May and hitting a career high of No. 156 as a result.

The Chinese 28-year-old scored a pair of remarkable victories in Wuhan. In the first round, she escaped Sorana Cirstea from 6-1, 4-0 down, saving triple match point to notch her first Top 20 win. Guo followed that by outlasting Katie Volynets in 3 hours and 4 minutes, the second-longest main-draw match of the tournament (behind Volynets' own 3-hour, 6-minute first-round win over Kimberly Birrell).

She returns to the Top 200 with a 51-place leap from No. 240 to No. 189.

Andreescu, Burel, Geerlings boosted by WTA 125 titles

Three WTA 125 tournaments took place last week -- on indoor hard courts in Rovereto, Italy and on clay in Lisbon, Portugal and Mallorca, Spain.

In Rovereto, the unseeded Bianca Andreescu claimed her biggest title since winning the 2019 US Open, coming from 4-1 down in the final to defeat 22-year-old Czech Dominika Salkova 7-6(2), 6-2. The Canadian also upset No. 1 seed Antonia Ruzic 7-5, 3-6, 7-5 in a 3-hour, 24-minute second-round tilt.

Andreescu, who also won two World Tennis events in January and reached the Austin WTA 125 final in March, improved her overall 2026 record to 35-18, and rises 36 places from No. 168 to No. 132. Salkova moves up four to a new career high of No. 112.

Meanwhile, Poland's Martyna Kubka climbs 19 places to a new career high of No. 247 and Czechia's Lucie Havlickova is up 23 places to No. 181 after reaching the Rovereto semifinals.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Plopp: Tennis BZ & TN 🎾🥎 | powered by Spitaler Sports (@plopp_tennis)

In Lisbon, former No. 42 Clara Burel collected her second straight WTA 125 trophy following Valencia last month, extending her winning streak to 10 matches by defeating Leyre Romero Gormaz 6-4, 6-3 in the final.

The Frenchwoman returned from a 12-month layoff due an ACL injury in April, unranked, and lost her first four matches back -- but has compiled a 26-7 record since June and did not drop a set in Lisbon. Burel returns to the Top 200 this week, vaulting 58 places from No. 214 to No. 158, and Romero Gormaz climbs 10 spots to No. 129.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Clara (@claraburel_)

In Mallorca, No. 505-ranked wild card Ariana Geerlings swept through a remarkable title run on home soil without the loss of a set. Like Burel, Geerlings was sidelined for a year (between July 2025 and July 2026) due to an ACL injury, but the Spaniard has compiled a 29-5 record since her return.

Her run in Mallorca included a 7-6(4), 6-3 second-round upset of No. 1 seed Julia Grabher, her first Top 100 win, and a 6-2, 6-2 defeat of 18-year-old No. 2 seed Laura Samson in the final. Geerlings soars 204 places to No. 301 this week -- just 11 places beneath the career high of No. 290 she set just after getting injured in 2025 -- and Samson moves 12 spots to No. 116.

Meanwhile, former Roland Garros semifinalist Tamara Zidansek climbs 18 places to No. 143 and Malta's Francesca Curmi jumps 25 places to a new career high of No. 208 after making the Mallorca semifinals.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Ariana Geerlings (@arianageerlings_)

Other notable rankings movements

Ashlyn Krueger, +13 to No. 55: Krueger reached the third round of Wuhan as a lucky loser.

Yulia Putintseva, +13 to No. 66: Putintseva qualified and made the second round of Wuhan.

Kristina Liutova, +6 to No. 110: Sixteen-year-old Memphis champion Liutova extended her 2026 record to 40-6 by reaching the Edmond W100 final last week. The teenager's 6-1, 6-3 semifinal defeat of Renata Zarazua extended her unbeaten career record against Top 100 opposition to 4-0.

Sloane Stephens, +15 to No. 118: Former US Open champion Stephens claimed her first title at any level since Rouen 2024, and her first on the World Tennis circuit since the 2011 Reggio Emilia W50, at last week's Edmond W100. Stephens' run included a 6-2, 6-3 defeat of 36-year-old Madison Brengle in the second round -- the pair's first meeting since 2011 Estoril qualifying -- then a pair of wins over up-and-coming teenagers in the last two rounds. Stephens, 33, edged 17-year-old Julieta Pareja 2-6, 6-1, 7-6(5) in the semifinals then topped Liutova 6-3, 6-2 in the final.

Shi Han, +40 to No. 177: After qualifying for Beijing and taking eventual champion Zheng Qinwen to three sets in the first round, Shi continued her surge in Wuhan. The Chinese 21-year-old scored her first two Top 100 wins, over Peyton Stearns and Kamilla Rakhimova to qualify again -- then took out Alexandra Eala in the first round for a maiden Top 20 upset.

Kajsa Rinaldo Persson, +24 to No. 223: The 28-year-old Swede captured her second career W50 title last week in Québec City.

Julieta Pareja, +22 to No. 228: Former junior No. 1 Pareja is up to a new career high after making the Edmond W100 semifinals.

Ipek Oz, +49 to No. 271: Former No. 163 Oz backed up her run to the Heraklion W50 final two weeks ago by winning last week's Stara Zagora W50, the 27-year-old's first title at that level.

Dana Guzman, +67 to No. 462: University of Oklahoma engineering graduate Guzman upset Caroline Dolehide and top seed Tatjana Maria to make the Edmond W100 quarterfinals, the latter her maiden Top 100 win. The Peruvian 23-year-old climbs to a new career high.

Ena Shibahara, +94 to No. 492: After being sidelined by an elbow injury for four months this year, former No. 116 Shibahara picked up the title in the third tournament of her return, the Wagga Wagga W35 two weeks ago.

Maaya Rajeshwaran Revathi, +347 to No. 726: The Indian 17-year-old collected her first professional title two weeks ago at the W35 in Lagos, Portugal. A semifinalist at the 2025 Mumbai WTA 125, Rajeshwaran Revathi qualified in Lagos and came from 5-0 down in the first set to upset top seed Justina Mikulskyte 7-6(1), 6-1 in the first round.

content.title: Former US Open champions Andreescu, Stephens climb rankings with titles
content.description: Bianca Andreescu and Sloane Stephens won titles in Rovereto, Italy and Oklahoma, USA, respectively, as the former US Open champions continued their push back up the rankings. Andreescu climbed 36 places to No. 132, while Stephens rose 15 spots to No. 118 after securing their biggest title wins in recent seasons.

related.label: Chwalinska’s breakout season reaches new heights with a WTA 1000 title in Wuhan
Elina Svitolina secures seventh singles spot for WTA Finals Indian Wells, one place remains
Kartal’s comeback gathers pace with landmark run to Wuhan final

content.body:
Former US Open champions Bianca Andreescu and Sloane Stephens captured titles over the weekend, boosting their rankings as they move closer to a return to the WTA top 100.

Andreescu, aged 26, rallied from 5-2 down in the first set to defeat sixth-seeded Dominika Salkova 7-6(2), 6-2 in the final to win the Rovereto Open Città della Pace, a WTA 125 event in Italy. It was the third win over a seeded player for the 2019 US Open champion, who also defeated top seed Antonia Ruzic and fifth seed Lucrezia Stefanini earlier in the week.

The title was Andreescu’s biggest of the season and her most significant since winning the 2019 US Open, her only Grand Slam singles title to date. She had also won ITF W35 and W75 titles in the first two months of the season. The victory marked her 12th professional singles title across all levels.

Andreescu climbed 36 places to No. 132 in this week’s rankings, her highest position since reaching No. 127 in April.

Meanwhile, in Edmond, Oklahoma, 2017 US Open champion Stephens defeated 16-year-old Kristina Liutova to win the ITF W100 Edmond title. It was Stephens’ first title since winning the WTA 250 event in Rouen in 2024 and her 11th professional singles title across all levels.

Stephens rose 15 places to No. 118 in this week’s rankings after beginning the season outside the top 1,000. It is also her highest ranking since February 2025.

content.title: Life after Roland Garros: How Chwalinska embraced the tough moments and won in Wuhan
content.description: In the few months that followed Roland Garros, Maja Chwalinska had to learn how to handle a whole new level of attention, but a strong Asian swing and a first WTA 1000 title in Wuhan show how far she has come.

related.label: Chwalinska’s breakout season reaches new heights with a WTA 1000 title in Wuhan
Elina Svitolina secures seventh singles spot for WTA Finals Indian Wells, one place remains
Martina Navratilova at 70: Her life in photos

content.body:
WUHAN -- For Maja Chwalinska, the pressure of reaching the Roland Garros final came after the tournament ended. Her run from qualifying elevated her from No. 114 to No. 21 and brought a level of attention she found difficult to manage.

“Miserable” is how she described feeling during the North American Hard-Court swing, when expectations from social media, the press and elsewhere began to weigh on her. After injuring herself on match point in a first-round loss at Wimbledon, she won just one match before another first-round exit at the US Open.

"It was very tough for me," Chwalinska told wtatennis.com after winning Wuhan on Sunday. "It's just such a different world for me now. Tennis stays the same, but off court it's just so much different. Great things are happening, but also it's just different with the attention, with the media. Everyone can speak and it's very challenging."

After taking time to adjust to the attention and refocusing on tennis, she began to feel better in Singapore, she said. The Asian swing proved a welcome reset for the new No. 11 in the PIF WTA Rankings, who is 9-2 since arriving on the continent.

A few weeks after reaching the Singapore semifinals, she won the Dongfeng • Voyah Wuhan Open, adding a WTA 1000 title to her breakthrough season.

The Wuhan title reinforced what Chwalinska began to believe at Roland Garros: She can compete with the world’s best on any surface. After a difficult summer, she has found her footing again and is adding to a season on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz that began with a more modest goal -- cracking the top 100.

"I'm just a human," Chwalinska said to press. "So I needed to admit [after French Open] was very tough for me, but I kept working really hard. I'm just very grateful that my work paid off today."

After the final, Chwalinska sat down with wtatennis.com to discuss her belief in herself and her journey in Wuhan. Here's more from that conversation:

You said Roland Garros gave you belief. When you were outside the Top 140 earlier this year, how hard was it to trust that your game could take you this far?

Chwalinska: It's very individual, but for me, it was more about my game style. I wasn't sure if my game can compete against the best of the world because it's not very common. I think that was the biggest question mark for me.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by WTA (@wta)

I know how much you enjoy the clay, but did winning Wuhan feel you proved your game also suits hard courts?

Chwalinska: I think so. 

I could hear the voices of others that I'm only good on clay, but I feel people sometimes are just trolls, and they just want to speak because no one listens to them, and they abort. It's tough because you're out there and you're just very vulnerable. You can say nothing back.

I'm definitely very happy that I proved to myself the most that I can play on every surface, can be very good and can win on every surface as well.

You're now ranked No. 11 in the world, and there's a lot of opportunity ahead of you with the remainder of this season and the start to 2027. How do you approach being in a great spot going forward?

Chwalinska: I feel my mentality won't change because it works for me. I just want to give my best, just want to win every single match and have no regrets. I just want to give my all.

If I win, it's great. If I lose, that's how it's supposed to be, I guess. I won't really think about the rankings at this moment, and honestly, I've never really been good with ranking goals. It doesn't really motivate me at all. I just try to focus on what I can improve in my game and also in myself.

In China, a lot of the fans like give players nicknames. Have you learned yours, and what do you think of it?

Chwalinska: Moon sister. Honestly, why not? [laughing]

Presenting your 2026 Wuhan Champion 🏆 #dongfengvoyahwuhanopen https://t.co/e0rEXUw9PN

— wta (@WTA) October 18, 2026

After your semifinal against Iga Swiatek, an interview you did together at 15 in Stockholm resurfaced on social media. You talked then about conquering the tour. What was it like to see that interview again and reflect on how far you’ve come?

Chwalinska: It's very sweet. When you are a kid, you just dream about great things, and it's just very cool to see now what we've done. Obviously Iga has won everything and has dominated the tour for many years.

I'm not complaining. I know what my journey has been, and I'm very grateful for what I've done also.

It's a very cool story. We're the same age. We're from the same country. We've been basically playing tournaments together since we were 10 years old. I think it's not that common, especially from Poland. It's not a tennis country yet. Hopefully, it will change, but it's a great story for us and for our country as well.

content.title: Three teams secure places in the WTA Finals Indian Wells doubles field
content.description: Elise Mertens and Zhang Shuai punched their ticket with the Australian Open title, while Kristina Mladenovic and Guo Hanyu, Cristina Bucsa and Nicole Melichar-Martinez also booked spots, leaving three places still open.
content.body:
• Kristina Mladenovic, who has twice won the event, has secured her place with partner Guo Hanyu
  • Cristina Bucsa is celebrating her debut qualification with Nicole Melichar-Martinez, who will be making her fifth WTA Finals appearance
  • Defending WTA Finals champion Elise Mertens has qualified with the highly experienced Zhang Shuai
  • Tickets are available here for this year's WTA Finals at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden

The WTA announced Monday that three doubles teams -- Guo Hanyu & Kristina Mladenovic, Cristina Bucsa & Nicole Melichar-Martinez and Elise Mertens & Zhang Shuai -- have qualified for the WTA Finals Indian Wells, leaving three qualification places remaining to compete on tennis' ultimate stage. 

The teams will join PIF Doubles WTA World No. 1 Katerina Siniakova & trailblazer Taylor Townsend, along with Canada’s Gabriela Dabrowski & Brazilian Luisa Stefani, in the doubles draw. Siniakova and Townsend, along with Dabrowski and Stefani, secured their participation earlier this season.

Following a knee injury, Aleksandra Krunic and her partner Anna Danilina (who currently occupy the No. 3 position on the PIF Race to the WTA Finals Leaderboard) have unfortunately been forced to withdraw from this year’s event.

Kristina Mladenovic is returning to the WTA Finals for the first time since 2019, when she secured her second title at the event after winning her first WTA Finals crown in 2018 (both with Timea Babos).

She and partner Guo Hanyu, who will be making her debut at the event, have won two titles this season, kicking off the year with a triumph at the WTA 250 ASB Classic (Auckland) before enjoying success on the grass of The Championships, Wimbledon.

Cristina Bucsa and Nicole Melichar-Martinez will also be making their debut as a team at the WTA Finals having enjoyed an impressive 2026 season on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz.

Bucsa, who will be stepping out at the WTA Finals for the first time, and Melichar-Martinez (making her fifth appearance, earning a runner-up finish in 2023) won the WTA 500 Guadalajara Open presented by Santander and also enjoyed success at the WTA 1000 level, contesting the title match at the Internazionali BNL d'Italia (Rome) and making the semifinals at the BNP Paribas Open (Indian Wells).

Elise Mertens and Zhang Shuai have qualified for the WTA Finals for the first time as a team, but they have no shortage of experience at the event, with a combined total of nine previous appearances between them. Mertens is a two-time champion, winning the title in 2022 and 2025 (both with Veronika Kudermetova) while 2026 marks Zhang Shuai’s third appearance.

Their season has been highlighted by winning the Australian Open, ensuring their qualification through the Grand Slam rule, while they also enjoyed a semifinal run at the WTA 1000 Miami Open presented by Itaú and a further quarterfinal appearance at the WTA 500 VANDA Pharmaceuticals Berlin Tennis Open.

The WTA Finals Indian Wells features the Top 8 singles and doubles teams on the PIF Race to the WTA Finals Leaderboard https://www.wtatennis.com/rankings/race-singles (with the 8th spot going to the singles player and doubles team that have won a Grand Slam if ranked No.8 to No.20). This showcases the world’s best singles players and doubles teams competing in a round-robin format with the singles champion lifting the WTA Finals Billie Jean King Trophy and the doubles champions earning the WTA Finals Martina Navratilova Trophy. The prestigious season-ending tournament celebrates the best of the WTA on and off the court, delivering an unrivaled fan experience that blends sport, entertainment and culture.

Tickets are available here https://www.wtatennis.com/tournaments/wta-finals/tickets for this year's WTA Finals at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden, one of the sport's premier destinations and tournament locations.

content.title: Chwalinska’s breakout season reaches new heights with a WTA 1000 title in Wuhan
content.description: Maja Chwalinska completed another breakthrough week in Wuhan, rallying from a set down to defeat Sonay Kartal and capture her first WTA title.

related.label: Dabrowski, Stefani capture Wuhan doubles crown, third title in a row
Elina Svitolina secures seventh singles spot for WTA Finals Indian Wells, one place remains
Ningbo draw: Rybakina returns; Kostyuk, Swiatek still in WTA Finals hunt

content.body:
It hadn't always been smooth sailing for Maja Chwalinska since her breakthrough at Roland Garros earlier this year, but the 25-year-old proved her run to the final in Paris was no fluke with another remarkable week in Wuhan, capturing her first career title. 

The No. 16 seed rallied from a set and a break down and faced a critical juncture at 4-all in the second set before forcing a decider. She then won the final five games -- saving three break points while serving for the match -- to defeat World No. 170 Sonay Kartal 2-6, 6-4, 6-2 in 2 hours, 43 minutes and lift the 2026 Dongfeng · Voyah Wuhan Open trophy.

"It means a lot. It tastes very sweet, I [must] admit," Chwalinska said in her post-match press conference. "I feel like I still don't realize that I won. So I feel like I just need a few days. But it feels special because after the French Open it was obviously amazing, but then I had some tough moments. I feel like people also were very rough towards me.

"And it took a toll on me as well. I'm just a human. So I need to admit it was very tough for me, but I kept working really hard. And I'm just very grateful that my hard work paid off today."

Chwalinska is the fourth player on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz since the format's introduction in 2009 to win her first title at the WTA 1000 level, joining Naomi Osaka (Indian Wells 2018), Bianca Andreescu (Indian Wells 2019) and Victoria Mboko (Montreal 2025).

She is also the fourth player to win a first WTA 1000 title this season, following Karolina Muchova (Doha), Marta Kostyuk (Madrid) and Zheng Qinwen (Beijing).

CHAMPION IN WUHAN 🏆 Maja Chwalinska seals the victory and claims her first WTA 1000 title after defeating Kartal in three sets 2-6, 6-4, 6-2. #dongfengvoyahwuhanopen https://t.co/UZOeMbcJKY

— wta (@WTA) October 18, 2026

The title carried added significance. Chwalinska became the first left-hander to win a WTA 1000 title since Petra Kvitova in Miami in 2023 and just the third Polish player to claim a WTA 1000 crown, after Agnieszka Radwanska and Iga Swiatek. She defeated Swiatek in the semifinals en route to the title.

Swiatek was just one piece of a challenging championship puzzle for Chwalinska, who came from a set down against Marie Bouzkova in the second round before defeating No. 10 seed Iva Jovic and former World No. 3 Maria Sakkari to reach the semifinals.

There, she rallied once again in the first all-Polish semifinal at a WTA-level event in the Open Era, saving two set points and winning the final four games of the opening set from 5-3 down before completing a straight-sets victory.

In the final, it appeared as if Maja's magic had finally run out when Kartal broke for a 2-0 lead in the second set. The Brit then saved four break points in her next service game, prompting a brief moment of frustration from Chwalinska, before the Pole converted her fifth break-point opportunity to get back on serve.

"I feel like my energy level was very low at the beginning," Chwalinska said. "But also, Sonay played amazing. I think she didn't let me play my best tennis, so all credit to her for not letting me play [well]. I feel like I gradually started to play much better, much more aggressive, I would say.

"Also, the depth of my shots improved. So I didn't feel well at the beginning, but what I'm proud of is the fighting spirit."

After winning the 71-minute second set, Chwalinska secured the decisive break for 3-2 in the third. A flurry of down-the-line winners and her patented "drop lob" combo then helped carry her to the biggest title of her career.

What a MOMENT for Maja 🤯 Maja Chwalinska claims her maiden WTA 1000 title in Wuhan! #dongfengvoyahwuhanopen https://t.co/o0F3gmaF5l

— wta (@WTA) October 18, 2026

The result lifts Chwalinska to a projected career-high No. 11 in the PIF WTA Rankings after starting the week at No. 22. Kartal is also expected to make a significant jump, climbing 121 spots from No. 170 to No. 49 after a six-month layoff due to a back injury that sent her ranking tumbling.

"I don't predict the future so I don't know what the future will bring," Chwalinska said. "But I'm for sure very grateful for this place now. I started the season, I think, ranked like 140 and my goal was to be Top 100 this year. I think I did a pretty good job. And I'm very grateful for that.

"But I feel like there's so much more to improve in my game and in myself. So that keeps me working."
content.author: WTA Staff
content.summary: Maja Chwalinska completed another breakthrough week in Wuhan, rallying from a set down to defeat Sonay Kartal and capture her first WTA title.
