content.title: Zheng Qinwen's maturing perspective on success fuels energizing Beijing run
content.description: Zheng Qinwen's latest run in Beijing is more than just the result. Returning to the site of a 2025 low point, she reflected on how subsequent lows reshaped her mindset and taught her to find value ahead of the final stretch of the 2026 season.
content.body:
BEIJING -- Zheng Qinwen used to think winning was like "water."

Every single match, she had to win because earlier in her career, winning was viewed as essential and a necessity to sustain life on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz. Winning was seen as the norm, and that made it difficult navigating low points at times. 

Now, particularly over the past few months, that viewpoint has changed. A day after she celebrated her 24th birthday, Zheng spoke on her maturing mindset as she enters her second career China Open semifinal following her win over Elina Svitolina in Friday's quarterfinal.

"I'm more grateful for every win because I understand how much effort I have made behind every win," Zheng said. "I've learned to enjoy the wins and the effort on court."

Of course, winning is important for rankings, prize money and capturing titles, but Zheng isn't riding or dying on it. Rather, she's come to appreciate the work behind the scenes and that low points in her career are not a negative thing, a lesson that she learned over the past few months. 

"My biggest takeaway is that lows are not necessarily bad," Zheng said. "Being positive every day is really difficult. When I am low, I have the energy to make a breakthrough. I saw the shortcomings in myself. I saw the weaknesses of my personality. The lows actually helped me improve.

"When you are in the lows, you should face the challenge. That's what helps you reflect and grow because you'll always make it back from the lows."

The China Open is particularly personal to Zheng, not just because she's performing in front of her home crowd, but rather it was the location of one of her lows last season. 

In Beijing in 2025, she retired from her third-round match with a right-elbow injury that had kept her out since Wimbledon because of the surgery. After that retirement, she didn't play again until Doha in February.

Eventually, because she wasn't playing at her highest level and getting results, the former World No. 4's ranking slipped to as low as No. 160 and she became reliant on wild cards for direct entry.

Then came Toronto, where a qualifying loss sparked the turning point of her season arguably when Zheng was at her lowest. At the push of her team, Zheng underwent an intense training block in Florida to rediscover her game and skipped Cincinnati. Since, she's posted her two best results all season with quarterfinals at the US Open and is now into the final four in Beijing. 

Simply, Zheng just needed to accept to herself that winning wasn't essential at that point in her time, and it's paid off. Zheng is 12-1 in main-draw matches since Toronto, including the three US Open qualifiers.

"What I did in that training block is still unforgettable," Zheng said. "I couldn't play those tournaments. I [had] to accept [that] I needed this training block. I need to accept when the coach, they are hard to me on court.

"I remember [my coach] Pere [Riba], he said to me: 'Right now you are just 140 in the ranking. You used to be 65 before. You need to listen to me more on court because you are not the top 10 you [once were].' I was really angry inside. But I have to calm down and say yes, that's the reality. Seems like the effort [has paid off]."

" When you are in the lows, you should face the challenge. That's what helps you reflect and grow because you'll always make it back from the lows. "
Zheng Qinwen during her post-quarterfinal press conference in Beijing

At the time, Zheng didn't expect that the results would come this quickly, admitting she was "too low" to look at the future. 

Experiencing low points is a part of every tennis player's career, and Zheng is no different. However, with her recovery and journey back onto the WTA Tour taking longer than expected, it made her appreciate the larger picture.

"Going through this journey, there have been many chapters. I could write many chapters," Zheng said. "You see the lows in the recent period, but in my junior years, there were many highs and lows. It's been like this all the way through.

"I didn't expect that the lows this time continued that long. That is why I treasure the opportunities now."
content.author: Cole Bambini
content.summary: Zheng Qinwen's latest run in Beijing is more than just the result. Returning to the site of a 2025 low point, she reflected on how subsequent lows reshaped her mindset and taught her to find value ahead of the final stretch of the 2026 season.

content.title: Serena Williams honored with Barbie doll to celebrate 2005 AO win
content.description: Serena Williams joins Team Barbie with a new doll inspired by her iconic 2005 Australian Open look, celebrating her legacy and inspiring young girls to dream big and break barriers.

related.label: Serena Williams gets a Barbie for International Women's Day
I want to represent people who think they aren’t represented – Osaka honored by Barbie Shero
Venus Williams' fight for equal pay celebrated with Barbie doll
'Just unbelievable!' Serena answers Routliffe's smash with screaming winner

content.body:
On International Day of the Girl, Serena Williams is inspiring young girls to dream big and believe they can be anything -- and she's got a new Barbie doll to prove it. The 23-time Grand Slam singles champion and tennis legend is officially joining Team Barbie, and getting her likeness celebrated amongst a group of athletes and role models that inspire confidence in young girls.

Harkening back to Williams' on-court outfit for her iconic 2005 Melbourne title run, where she famously saved match points in the semifinal against Maria Sharapova, Williams' doll wears a green and white cutout top with mesh detailing and a white skirt. It also includes matching tennis shoes, socks, a sweatband, a racquet and a tennis ball.

“Growing up, I didn’t see many girls who looked like me being told there was no limit to who they could become," Williams said in a press release. "I want every girl who plays with this doll to see possibility -- not just in me, but in herself. She can dream big, work hard, change direction, break barriers, and become anything she chooses. That’s what makes having my own Barbie so meaningful to me."

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Barbie (@barbie)

Williams said Mattel "nailed" her outfit from two decades ago, and was thrilled to have her hairstyle of the time accurately captured too.

“I was really adamant about having big curly hair and having a little color in the hair as well,” she said.

It's not the first time that Williams is getting a doll in her likeness. Earlier this year in celebration of International Women's Day, the former World No. 1 was named part of the "Barbie Dream Team" to celebrate her post-playing career as an entrepreneur, after previously getting a doll in her likeness made earlier in the aughts. 

"Barbie is proud to honor Serena Williams. Barbie has always inspired girls to believe they can be anything, from the sports stadium to the fashion runway to the boardroom," Nathan Baynard, vice president and head of Barbie, Mattel, said in a statement. "Serena Williams embodies that message through her extraordinary achievements as an athlete, entrepreneur, and advocate for equality.

"By honoring her with a Barbie Signature doll, we’re celebrating a barrier-breaking icon whose legacy empowers fans everywhere to dream big and embrace their own potential."
content.author: WTA Staff
content.subtitle: Social Buzz
content.summary: Serena Williams joins Team Barbie with a new doll inspired by her iconic 2005 Australian Open look, celebrating her legacy and inspiring young girls to dream big and break barriers.

content.title: Eala talks perfection, embracing pain and brutal feedback with Sharapova
content.description: Alexandra Eala was a guest on "Pretty Tough with Maria Sharapova," and the World No. 18 went in-depth on a number of topics, including carrying the hopes of a nation and what makes her feel tough.

related.label: Third time's the charm: Andreeva tops Alexandrova to reach Beijing semis
Shnaider, Cirstea, Eala, Paolini headline Hong Kong field
First WTA 1000 semifinal! Bartunkova beats Muchova in 67 minutes in Beijing

content.body:
Ever since first emerging on the scene in March 2025, when she made a surprise run to the Miami semifinals as a wild card, Alexandra Eala has continued to ascend.

As she's grown into one of the biggest stars on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz, and had to manage expectations and a fiercely devoted global fan base, she's backed it up with results. She ended last season outside the Top 50 of the PIF WTA Rankings, and as the season weaves its way through its final swing she finds herself in the Top 20.

Her crowning achievement was her first title this past summer in Washington, D.C., where she beat Elina Svitolina, Naomi Osaka and Jessica Pegula in succession to win the WTA 500 tournament.

There have been obstacles, of course. A first-round loss to Alycia Parks in Melbourne, a subpar Clay-Court Swing, a heartbreaking loss to Iva Jovic at the US Open and, most recently, a surprising defeat to then-World No. 180 Tatiana Prozorova in Singapore.

But that's par for the course. Adversity is inevitable, and Eala's ability to handle it with maturity and perspective is one of the reasons she's been so successful.

"I think one thing that I've learned in the past couple of months about myself is my capacity to suffer," Eala said on "Pretty Tough with Maria Sharapova," the five-time Grand Slam champion's podcast. "And [to] be in those situations where you're uncomfortable and you're out of breath and you're nervous.

"And of course it's always easier to enjoy when you're winning, and when you're winning you forget what it feels like to be losing consecutively. But recently, I've been almost looking forward to those moments where I'm out of breath, or those moments where I'm really nervous. And I've learned to enjoy facing them head on."

Eala and Sharapova discussed a wide range of topics on the hour-long podcast, from carrying the hopes of a nation to her experience at the Rafa Nadal Academy to what makes her feel pretty and tough.

Eala's appearance on "Pretty Tough with Maria Sharapova" continues a busy off-court stretch for the World No. 18, which also included three shows at New York Fashion Week and the Chanel Spring/Summer 2027 show at Paris Fashion Week.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Alexandra Eala (@alex.eala)

Eala will return to WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz action next week in Wuhan, the final WTA 1000 tournament of the season.

content.title: China Open semifinals preview: Breaking down the final four in Beijing
content.description: Mirra Andreeva will take on rising star Nikola Bartunkova in the first China Open semifinal, and then wild card Zheng Qinwen will play Elise Mertens. We break down both matchups in Beijing.

related.label: Mertens beats Swiatek in Beijing for third straight win over a Grand Slam champion
The first-timers who won the WTA Finals: Could Andreeva or Noskova be next?
Mirra Andreeva and Linda Noskova secure qualification for WTA Finals Indian Wells

content.body:
And then there were four.

The China Open quarterfinalists were a rather unlikely final eight, with only one top five seed among them. The semifinalists are even more surprising, with only one player inside the Top 15, a wild card and three players looking for their first career WTA 1000 title.

Home favorite Zheng Qinwen upset sixth-seeded Elina Svitolina to book her semifinal spot. She'll take on Elise Mertens, who beat Iga Swiatek for the first time.

In the second semifinal, Mirra Andreeva, fresh off her first WTA Finals qualification, will play rising star Nikola Bartunkova. Andreeva beat Ekaterina Alexandrova in the quarterfinals, and Bartunkova upset fellow Czech Karolina Muchova.

Here's everything you need to know ahead of the semifinals in Beijing.

[WC] Zheng Qinwen vs. [13] Elise Mertens

Zheng leads the head-to-head 1-0

While the rest of the top players on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz were competing in Cincinnati in August, Zheng was down in Florida, having a much-needed training block. The decision to skip Cincinnati to get right for the rest of the season proved to be a fruitful one. The former World No. 4 came through qualifying to reach the US Open quarterfinals, and has exceeded that result in Beijing, reaching the semis as a wild card. She's often taken the scenic route to wins in Beijing, as she did in New York, with three-set victories in each of her first four matches.

Friday's quarterfinal against Svitolina, her toughest opponent to date in Beijing, told a different story. Zheng mercifully won in straights, setting the tone for the match with an early break. She would break twice more in the opening set to take the lead. Both players held until the tiebreak in the second, but Zheng came up clutch in the tiebreaker, consistent with her theme over the past two months. 

Coming into this match, nine of Zheng's last 10 matches had gone to a third set, so she's well-equipped to win when it's late and close. She's won 12 of her last 13 matches overall.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by WTA (@wta)

She'll face Mertens, who's also had some close calls in Beijing. She trailed by a break in the third set against Katie Volynets in her first match, and also needed three to get past Jelena Ostapenko. But she's gotten stronger and more confident with every match, and that was evident in straight-set wins over multiple-time Grand Slam champions Coco Gauff and Swiatek. In the 7-6 (0), 6-3 win over Swiatek on Friday, Mertens was highly efficient on serve, winning 87 percent of her first-serve points. She was equally effective on the return, never giving Swiatek the opportunity to break.

Mertens is into her first WTA 1000 semifinal in five years, when she reached the final four in Dubai in 2021. She's made this stage three times at WTA 1000s, but never won a title. She's pulling double duty, as she so often does, and will play the doubles semifinal on Saturday alongside Diana Shnaider. 

But the top priority, she told reporters after the match, is Zheng.

"Recovery is key," she said. "Eat, sleep and repeat the same. Yeah, just focus on the singles first. That's definitely the goal."

Zheng and Mertens have played once before, in Charleston last year. Zheng won that match 6-3, 3-6, 6-3.

[4] Mirra Andreeva vs. [26] Nikola Bartunkova

Andreeva leads the head-to-head 1-0

Bartunkova is having the tournament of her young career.

The latest in a long line of established and rising Czech stars, the 20-year-old took out World No. 2 Aryna Sabalenka last week, the biggest win of her career, and has carried that momentum into her first career WTA 1000 semifinal. (It's only her third career WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz semifinal.) The win over Sabalenka was stunningly routine, and so too was her quarterfinal win over countrywoman Karolina Muchova on Thursday.

Bartunkova started strong and finished even stronger, winning the first five games and the final seven games against the far more accomplished and experienced Muchova, 10 years her senior. The scoreline required a double take: 6-3, 6-0 in just 67 minutes. Bartunkova, who has often been compared to Muchova and knows her game very well, beat the World No. 8 at her own game, with variety, exceptional touch and the unique ability to hit any shot from anywhere on the court. Bartunkova was also aggressive, employing a first-strike mentality that didn't allow Muchova to get settled and dictate points. In the second game of the opening set, Bartunkova hit four consecutive deep returns to Muchova's feet, resulting in four errors and a quick break. That game gave her the early edge and she never looked back. 

Her semifinal opponent, Andreeva, also has the advantage in accolades. But unlike Muchova, she's actually older than the teenage Andreeva. The 19-year-old French Open champion has had a relatively smooth path to the semifinals, winning eight consecutive sets after dropping the opener in her first-round match. Andreeva needed two tiebreaks to get past Alexandrova on Thursday, her first win against the veteran in three tries, but it was murky at times. Alexandrova served for the opening set at 5-3 and later led 6-5, and Andreeva let a 5-2 lead slip away in the second. But she prevailed in the most crucial moments, winning five of the final six points in the second-set tiebreaker.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by WTA (@wta)

Andreeva had 23 errors to 16 unforced errors, including a sparkling 15-to-5 ratio in the second, and was opportunistic in her return games, converting four of her seven break-point opportunities.

It will be the second match between these two in as many months. Andreeva beat Bartunkova 6-2, 7-6 (5) in the third round of the US Open.

"Even though I won [at the] US Open, I still felt like the match was tough," Andreeva told reporters. "A lot of up and downs. I think this match is going to be very entertaining for people to watch. She's an amazing player. I'm super excited to play her again."
content.author: Brad Kallet
content.summary: Mirra Andreeva will take on rising star Nikola Bartunkova in the first China Open semifinal, and then wild card Zheng Qinwen will play Elise Mertens. We break down both matchups in Beijing.

content.body:
Top 20 players Diana Shnaider, Sorana Cirstea, Alexandra Eala and Jasmine Paolini will headline the field at next month's WTA 250 Prudential Hong Kong Tennis Open, one of the final two tournaments on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz calendar before the WTA Finals.

They'll be joined by Top 50 players Leylah Fernandez, Ann Li, Maria Sakkari, Cristina Bucsa, Talia Gibson, Wang Xinyu, Liudmila Samsonova, Kimberly Birrell, Yuliia Starodubtseva, Daria Snigur, Oleksandra Oliynykova and Anhelina Kalinina.

Rounding out the direct entry list is Mayar Sherif, Zheng Qinwen, Katie Boulter, Sonay Kartal, Zeynep Sonmez, Paula Badosa and Anna Bondar.

The first five main-draw alternates are Tereza Valentova, Camila Osorio, Viktorija Golubic, Maria Timofeeva and Alina Korneeva.

In addition to the 23 direct entrants, the 32-player singles draw includes four qualifiers, four wild cards and one special exempt spot. The top four seeds will get byes into the second round. The draw will be revealed on Saturday, Oct. 31.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Prudential Hong Kong Tennis Open (@hk_tennisopen)

Victoria Mboko, who has been out of action since June, is the defending champion in Hong Kong. She defeated Bucsa in a three-set final.

Shnaider won the tournament the year prior, defeating Boulter in the final, and Fernandez won it in 2023. Fernandez has also made the semifinals in Hong Kong in each of the last two years.

Played on outdoor hard courts at the Victoria Park Tennis Stadium, the Prudential Hong Kong Tennis Open dates back to 1980. After a 32-year hiatus -- minus one edition, in 1993 -- it returned to the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz in 2014.

First-round action in Hong Kong will kick off on Monday, Nov. 2, and the tournament will run through Sunday, Nov. 8, when the singles and doubles finals will be played.

The WTA 250 Chennai Open will take place on the same days.

The WTA Finals at Indian Wells will get underway on Nov. 8, just as these tournaments are concluding.

content.title: Third time's the charm: Andreeva tops Alexandrova to reach Beijing semis
content.description: Mirra Andreeva earned her first win over Ekaterina Alexandrova on Thursday night, edging the No. 19 seed 7-6 (4), 7-6 (3) to reach her first Beijing semifinal. She improved to 1-2 against Alexandrova and advanced to her fourth WTA 1000 semifinal.

related.label: First WTA 1000 semifinal! Bartunkova beats Muchova in 67 minutes in Beijing
Bartunkova’s year of growth continues to pay off with a semifinal run in Beijing
Zheng powers into Beijing last eight with three-set win over Charaeva

content.body:
They say the third time is the charm, and that proved true for Mirra Andreeva on Thursday night as she earned her first win over No. 19 seed Ekaterina Alexandrova 7-6 (4), 7-6 (3) in 1 hour and 53 minutes to reach the Beijing semifinals for the first time.

Beijing: Scores | Order of play | Draws

Andreeva led 4-1 and served for the match at 5-3 in the second set, but Alexandrova mounted a late comeback to force a tiebreak. There, Andreeva fired a forehand winner to take a 3-2 lead, let out a roar and won five of the final six points to seal the victory.

"Even when I had an advantage in the second set leading 5-2, I felt like she was still pressuring me," Andreeva said in her post-match interview. "I felt like she was playing better and I didn't take my chances. I could have played more aggressive, but what a match this was. I'm super happy with how it went.

"She played unbelievable today, and I'm very happy to get my very first win against her."

Big win in Beijing 🔥 Mirra Andreeva defeats Alexandrova to secure her semifinal place in Beijing and move a step closer in the race to WTA Finals Indian Wells! #ChinaOpen https://t.co/4Ek6z3Duj3

— wta (@WTA) October 8, 2026

With the win, Andreeva improved to 1-2 against Alexandrova at the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz level after failing to win a set in their previous two meetings. She also became the youngest player to reach the China Open semifinals since Agnes Szavay in 2007.

The result sends Andreeva into her fourth career WTA 1000 semifinal. Since the format's introduction in 2009, only Coco Gauff (five) has reached more WTA 1000 semifinals as a teenager.

Stat watch

The numbers heavily favored Andreeva despite the narrow margin on the scoreboard.

Into her first Beijing semifinal 🤩 Mirra Andreeva secures the win against Alexandrova! #ChinaOpen https://t.co/04TwsADZZN

— wta (@WTA) October 8, 2026

She landed 62% of her first serves and won 71% of those points while finishing with a positive winners-to-unforced-errors differential of 23-16, including a 15-5 mark in the second set. Both players broke serve four times, with Andreeva converting four of seven break-point opportunities and Alexandrova 4 of 10.

Andreeva's 296 break points converted are the most by any player in WTA main-draw matches in 2026. Only four players have hit more winners than Andreeva's 1,350 this season: Elena Rybakina, Aryna Sabalenka, Linda Noskova and Jessica Pegula.

Young stars set for battle

Andreeva will face Nikola Bartukova in the semis after the 20-year-old stunned compatriot Karolina Muchova 6-3, 6-0 in 67 minutes on Thursday to reach her first WTA 1000 semifinal.

It will be the second meeting between the rising stars. Their first came at the US Open last month, where Andreeva prevailed 6-2, 7-6 (5).

"She beat a lot of great players on her way to the semifinals," Andreeva told reporters. "For sure, this match will be tough. Even though I won at the US Open, I still felt like the match was tough. Lots of ups and downs. I think this match is going to be very entertaining for people to watch. She's an amazing player, so I'm super excited to play her again.

"She's also very young, so it's kind of a battle of -- I don't want to say new generation -- but young players."

At a combined age of 40 years, six days, Andreeva and Bartunkova will form the fourth-youngest WTA 1000 semifinal matchup since 2009. The only younger pairings were Iga Swiatek-Coco Gauff (Rome 2021), Ana Ivanovic-Anastasia Pavlyuchenkova (Indian Wells 2009) and Bianca Andreescu-Sofia Kenin (Toronto 2019).

The winner will face either No. 6 seed Elina Svitolina, No. 8 seed Iga Swiatek, No. 13 seed Elise Mertens or local favorite Zheng Qinwen in the final.

content.title: First WTA 1000 semifinal! Bartunkova beats Muchova in 67 minutes in Beijing
content.description: Nikola Bartunkova won an inter-generational clash of Czech compatriots against Karolina Muchova in just 67 minutes in the China Open quarterfinals, scoring her third Top 10 win and advancing to her first WTA 1000 semifinal.

related.label: Bartunkova’s year of growth continues to pay off with a semifinal run in Beijing
Zheng powers into Beijing last eight with three-set win over Charaeva
Wuhan 2026: Dates, draws, prize money and everything you need to know

content.body:
No. 26 seed Nikola Bartunkova reached the first WTA 1000 semifinal of her career on Thursday, defeating No. 7 Karolina Muchova 6-3, 6-0 in 67 minutes at the China Open.

In an inter-generational matchup of Czech compatriots who train at Prague’s Štvanice club, the 20-year-old Bartunkova won the first five and final seven games against the 30-year-old Muchova. It was her third career win over a Top 10 opponent, following victories over Belinda Bencic at the Australian Open and Aryna Sabalenka in the third round in Beijing. Bartunkova had previously reached tour-level semifinals in Guadalajara in 2025 and Monterrey in 2026.

Bartunkova, who ended 2025 ranked No. 130 and has climbed to No. 34 this week, will make her Top 30 debut following Beijing. She will bid to reach her first career final against No. 4 seed Mirra Andreeva, who narrowly escaped No. 19 Ekaterina Alexandrova 7-6(4), 7-6(3)

Despite her steep upward trajectory in 2026, Bartunkova's run in Beijing has taken her by surprise.

"For sure [I didn't expect it] before this tournament," she said in her press conference. "I played lot of practices with top players -- [iga] Swiatek, [Coco] Gauff, others. Maybe it helps little bit. [It] was one week before the tournament. I tried to play a lot of practices, lot of matches. I think that was the reason I had good preparation for this tournament. So yeah, I had confidence. But honestly I didn't expect these results."

How did Bartunkova pull off the upset?

As Bartunkova has risen through the rankings this year, her combination of power and touch has drawn frequent comparisons to Muchova herself. Ahead of their first meeting, the question was whether Muchova’s greater experience -- particularly during the most consistent season of her career, which has included titles in Doha and Bad Homburg and a second Grand Slam final at Wimbledon -- would give her the edge.

"I follow her a lot," said Bartunkova of Muchova. "I have also similar style like her, playing lot of drop shots, volleys. I like her because she's also a great human being."

Off court, there was respect. On court, Bartunkova didn't permit Muchova to get her game going. The younger player has every shot in the book, and a first-strike mentality to use them as quickly as possible in the point. She broke in the second game with four consecutive returns fired deep at Muchova's feet, drawing an error each time. In the fourth game, she used her drop shot as an audacious plus-one winner en route to breaking again.

The drop shot was also the setup for Bartunkova's two best points of the match -- a stretch backhand volley as she moved up 4-0 in the first set, and a perfect volleyed lob at the same stage of the second.

Intent on being the first to break open each point, Bartunkova did not let herself get drawn into extended rallies and within 20 minutes led 5-0.

"Today I was really aggressive," she said. "I [wasn't] very nervous. Yeah, try to put my best tennis. I did it."

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by WTA (@wta)

What were Muchova's best chances to turn the match around?

At 5-0 in the first set, Bartunkova was in such complete command that she even pulled off an absurd backhand slice winner that caught Muchova off guard yet again. But a handful of forehand errors allowed Muchova to get on the board, and closing out the set proved a tricky task.

Bartunkova has squandered a number of significant leads this summer -- 6-2, 4-0 against Sabalenka in Berlin; 5-1 in the third set and four match points against Lanlana Tararudee in Prague; 4-2 in the third set against Amanda Anisimova in Toronto; 6-1, 3-0 against Elise Mertens in Monterrey. Surely aware of that pattern, Muchova played her most aggressive tennis to claw back three games and fend off five set points.

But the gulf was too much to make up -- and, as Bartunkova said, her nerves didn't come into play. Up a sixth set point, Muchova offered up a drop shot that landed closer to the service line than the net, and Bartunkova stayed calm to swat it away for a winner.

There were no similar chances in the second set. Bartunkova leapt out to an early lead again and this time didn't let up, tallying 19 winners to Muchova's 12. Muchova faded in the home stretch as her unforced error count reached 37.
content.author: WTA Staff
content.summary: Nikola Bartunkova won an inter-generational clash of Czech compatriots against Karolina Muchova in just 67 minutes in the China Open quarterfinals, scoring her third Top 10 win and advancing to her first WTA 1000 semifinal.

content.title: Wuhan 2026: Dates, draws, prize money and everything you need to know
content.description: The 2026 season's last WTA 1000 event has arrived on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz. In Wuhan, here is the schedule, field, defending champions and what is at stake at the Dongfeng Voyah Wuhan Open

related.label: Coco Gauff, Naomi Osaka to miss Wuhan Open

content.body:
The 2026 Asian Swing continues with the season's last WTA 1000, the Dongfeng Voyah Wuhan Open.

Wuhan will play hosts to its ninth edition, and three-time champion Aryna Sabalenka headlines the field as the lone past champion set to compete. The tournament is played at the Optics Valley International Tennis Centre on outdoor hard courts. 

Here is everything to know about this year’s Wuhan Open.

What are the dates for each round?

Main-draw play begins Monday, Oct. 12, and concludes Sunday, Oct. 18 with the championships. The doubles final begins at 4:00 p.m. local time with the singles final to follow, not before 6:30 p.m.

Time conversions: 6:30 p.m. China Standard Time = 6:30 a.m. EST, 11:30 a.m. BST, 12:30 p.m. CEST

Here are the dates for each round:

Singles
First round: October 12-13
Second round: October 14
Third round: October 15
Quarterfinals: October 16
Semifinals: October 17
Final: October 18

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by 2026 DONGFENG •VOYAH WUHAN OPEN (@wuhanopenwta)

Doubles
First round: October 12-13
Second round: October 14-15
Quarterfinals: October 16
Semifinals: October 17
Final: October 18

What is the singles draw and who are some of the stars competing?

In Wuhan, there will be a 56-player singles field, one of three WTA 1000 tournaments with a draw of that size alongside Doha and Dubai. In doubles, the field is 28 teams.

With World No. 1 Elena Rybakina's withdrawal, Sabalenka will be the top ranked player in this year's edition, seeking to win her fourth Wuhan Open. She is the lone defending champion set to compete.

Jessica Pegula, 2025 finalist, is set to return to the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz for the first time since the US Open. Pegula is one of two past finalists, joining Zheng Qinwen, who advanced to the final in 2024. 

Mirra Andreeva, Linda Noskova, Elina Svitolina, Karolina Muchova, Iga Swiatek and Marta Kostyuk round out top eight seeds in the mix. They, in addition to Sabalenka and Pegula, will receive a bye into the second round. 

Projected seeded players

  1. Aryna Sabalenka
  2. Jessica Pegula
  3. Mirra Andreeva
  4. Linda Noskova
  5. Elina Svitolina
  6. Karolina Muchova
  7. Iga Swiatek
  8. Marta Kostyuk
  9. Belinda Bencic 
  10. Iva Jovic
  11. Diana Shnaider
  12. Sorana Cirstea
  13. Alexandra Eala
  14. Elise Mertens 
  15. Jasmine Paolini
  16. Maja Chwalinska

Draw ceremony: The singles draw ceremony will be held on Saturday, Oct. 10 at 4 p.m. local time.

Singles wild cards: To be determined

*Singles Withdrawals: Elena Rybakina (foot), Coco Gauff (fatigue), Amanda Anisimova (wrist) Naomi Osaka (change of schedule), Emma Navarro, Madison Keys (abdominal injury), Anastasia Potapova, Karolina Pliskova (back)

*Entry lists are subject to change. The full player list can be found here. 

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by 2026 DONGFENG •VOYAH WUHAN OPEN (@wuhanopenwta)

Who are the defending champions?

Last season, Gauff defeated Pegula 6-4, 7-5 in 1 hour and 42 minutes to earn her 11th of 12 WTA singles titles. Wuhan was her second championship of the 2025 season, more than four months after she won her second Grand Slam at Roland Garros. 

Gauff was consistent all week, defeating the ranks of Zhang Shaui, Jasmine Paolini and more. She won all her matches in straight sets, becoming the first player to win Wuhan without dropping a set since the tournament’s inception in 2014. Across her five matches, she lost just a total of 25 games, the fewest of any Wuhan champion.

In doubles, Katerina Siniakova and Storm Hunter defeated Aleksandra Krunic and Anna Danilina 6-3, 6-2 in the final. 

What are the ranking points and prize money at stake?

In Wuhan, a total of $4,088,211 is available in prize money. As with all WTA 1000 events, 1000 ranking points are on the table.

Any change in rank is based on how the player performs in the tournament compared to the points earned in the same week last year.

content.title: Coco Gauff, Naomi Osaka to miss Wuhan Open
content.description: Coco Gauff and Naomi Osaka will miss next week's Wuhan Open, the final WTA 1000 tournament of the season. Zheng Qinwen will replace Osaka in the draw.

related.label: Breaking down the unlikely quarterfinal matchups in Beijing
Mertens beats Gauff for first time in six meetings to make Beijing quarters

content.body:
Coco Gauff will miss next week's Dongfeng Voyah · Wuhan Open, the tournament has announced on social media. 

"I'm disappointed to withdraw from Wuhan, especially as the defending champion," Gauff said, according to an Instagram story posted by the tournament. "I always love playing there. After a long year, my body needs some time to rest and recover. I look forward to returning next year."

Gauff, who won the title in Wuhan last year without dropping a set, is coming off a run to the fourth round in Beijing. After back-to-back wins over Camila Osorio and junior World No. 1 Sun Xinran, Gauff struggled mightily against Elise Mertens on Wednesday. The World No. 4 had 34 unforced errors, including eight double faults.

"I think I just didn't play well," Gauff told reporters after the 6-3, 6-3 loss. "I think I wasn't moving well. There were a lot of things I didn't do well."

The 12-time WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz champion admitted that she was "just a bit flat," and was looking forward to getting some much-needed rest.

Gauff is currently fifth on the PIF WTA Race to the Finals leaderboard.

Naomi Osaka will also miss the Wuhan Open, the tournament announced. Like Gauff, Osaka made it to the Round of 16 in Beijing, losing to Karolina Muchova 7-5, 1-6, 7-6 (7) in a match that lasted 2 hours and 52 minutes. Osaka led by a break in both the first and third sets, but Muchova rallied before clinching the win on her ninth match point.

Home favorite Zheng Qinwen, still in the field in Beijing, will replace Osaka in the draw, the tournament announced.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by 2026 DONGFENG •VOYAH WUHAN OPEN (@wuhanopenwta)

In addition to Gauff and Osaka, World No. 1 Elena Rybakina and Amanda Anisimova will miss Wuhan, the final WTA 1000 tournament of the season. Aryna Sabalenka is projected to be the top seed. 

First-round action in Wuhan will begin on Monday, Oct. 12. The tournament will run through Sunday, Oct. 18, when both the singles and doubles finals will be played.

content.title: Zheng powers into Beijing last eight with three-set win over Charaeva
content.description: Zheng Qinwen continued her strong run on home soil, defeating Alina Charaeva 6-1, 2-6, 6-4 on Tuesday to reach the Beijing quarterfinals for the second time in four appearances. The victory sent her to a third WTA 1000 quarterfinal in China, where she will face Elina Svitolina.

related.label: Mertens beats Gauff for first time in six meetings to make Beijing quarters
By the numbers: Swiatek defeats Jovic to strengthen WTA 1000 record
Alexandra Eala steps out in Chanel at Paris Fashion Week

content.body:
Zheng Qinwen continued the strong form she displayed at last month's US Open, reaching her second consecutive quarterfinal with a 6-1, 2-6, 6-4 victory over Alina Charaeva on Tuesday in Beijing.

Beijing: Scores | Order of play | Draws

Zheng needed 2 hours and 11 minutes to advance to the Beijing quarterfinals for the second time in four appearances. Between Beijing and Wuhan, she has reached three WTA 1000 quarterfinals on home soil, tying Li Na and Zhang Shuai for the most by a Chinese player since the format was introduced in 1990.

The win was Zheng's first against Charaeva at the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz level and came one day before her 24th birthday.

Early birthday present secured ♥️ #ChinaOpen https://t.co/uwP3POtBmq

— wta (@WTA) October 7, 2026

"I'm just really appreciative to have won this match because [there were] some ups and downs," Zheng said in her post-match press conference. "But I'm just happy to be on court and in the end get the win because everybody knows it's my last day of [being] 23 years old.

"I hope my team prepared a good birthday gift for me."

Following a familiar pattern

Each of Zheng's four wins in Beijing have gone the distance, and three have followed a familiar script: win the first set, drop the second and rebound in the third. That was the case again Tuesday night.

Zheng won the opening set in dominant fashion, hitting 14 winners while Charaeva posted an improbable ratio of zero winners to unforced errors. But the script flipped in the second set, when Charaeva won all 14 of her first-serve points and converted both break-point opportunities to force a decider.

Zheng seized control early in the third set. The Olympic gold medalist raced to a 5-2 lead, then overcame a late break that brought Charaeva back on serve at 5-4 before her fifth break of the match sealed another three-set victory.

Fought through in three 💪 Zheng Qinwen defeats Charaeva for a place in the last eight in Beijing! #ChinaOpen https://t.co/rqFTvVdj7c

— wta (@WTA) October 7, 2026

Zheng has now won seven of her past eight three-set matches at tour level, with her only loss during that stretch coming against eventual champion Elena Rybakina at the US Open.

"I would say that physically I wasn't the best, but I'm still holding on," Zheng said. "I've had a lot of three-set matches. I got some good wins in the first set. I think I have to solve [how] to keep my consistency and focus longer, but I feel my endurance is quite good. Of course, there's always something I could improve physically."

First meeting with Svitolina awaits

Zheng will face No. 6 seed Elina Svitolina for the first time after the Ukrainian defeated No. 21 seed Ann Li 6-2, 6-3 in 1 hour and 31 minutes on Tuesday night to reach her 29th career WTA 1000 quarterfinal.

Took care of business 💼 @ElinaSvitolina is into her 29th career WTA 1000 quarterfinal after defeating Li! #ChinaOpen https://t.co/ddy7sV9O1A

— wta (@WTA) October 7, 2026

In doing so, Svitolina surpassed Karolina Pliskova for sole possession of 10th place on the all-time since the format's introduction in 2009. She also improved to 2-0 against Li in their career meetings.

Svitolina can reach a 17th career WTA 1000 semifinal when she faces Zheng in a highly anticipated first meeting. Zheng will seek her fourth WTA 1000 semifinal as she continues her pursuit of the biggest title of her career outside of the Olympics.

Zheng carries a formidable arsenal into the matchup. She has hit the most winners of any player at this year's China Open (151), and only three players have served more aces than Zheng (285) in WTA main-draw matches this season: Rybakina, Linda Noskova and Aryna Sabalenka.

content.title: Mertens beats Gauff for first time in six meetings to make Beijing quarters
content.description: Elise Mertens defeated Coco Gauff for the first time in six meetings to reach her first China Open quarterfinal.

related.label: By the numbers: Swiatek defeats Jovic to strengthen WTA 1000 record
'I was shaking!' Muchova edges Osaka on ninth match point in Beijing thriller
Bartunkova’s year of growth continues to pay off with a semifinal run in Beijing

content.body:
The sixth time was the charm for Elise Mertens in her rivalry with Coco Gauff.

No. 13 seed Mertens defeated No. 3 seed Gauff for the first time 6-3, 6-3 in the China Open fourth round, advancing to her first Beijing quarterfinal in her seventh appearance.

Despite trailing 0-5 in their head-to-head prior to Wednesday, Mertens had come close to beating Gauff before. In their first meeting, she led the then 17-year-old 6-0, 3-1 in the 2021 Eastbourne first round before falling 0-6, 7-6(4), 7-5. Eight months ago, she held three match points on Gauff in the Dubai third round, only for the American to escape 2-6, 7-6(9), 6-3.

This time, Mertens held on in impressive style, winning 10 of her last 11 service points and sealing victory with her second ace -- ironically, her first straightforward scoreline of the tournament so far. In the second round, she led Katie Volynets 6-0, 3-0 but ultimately needed to come from a break down in the decider to win 6-0, 4-6, 7-5 in 2 hours and 54 minutes. In the third round, she overturned a 2-0 third-set deficit to quell Jelena Ostapenko 6-2, 3-6, 6-4.

After sealing the win over Gauff, she revealed she had some extra motivation -- though it was more about romance than revenge.

"My coach/boyfriend [Christopher Heyman], it's his birthday tomorrow," she said in her on-court interview. "So for me, this win is dedicated to him."

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by WTA (@wta)

Gauff, the 2024 Beijing champion, delivered a flat performance, racking up 34 unforced errors in total. Eight of those were double faults, and four of those came as she dropped serve in the final game of the first set. Trailing 4-1 in the second set, Gauff told her team courtside that she had "no energy" and felt as though she would pass out.

Mertens had also noticed this, but was taking nothing for granted -- especially having twice lost to Gauff after holding significant leads. Her hold for 4-1, in which she had navigated two deuces, had felt crucial.

"I kind of felt like she was dropping a bit in energy," Mertens said. "I tried to push myself. But I know she's a great competitor. It's never done against her."

The result is Mertens' 10th career Top 5 win, and her second of 2026 following her upset of Elena Rybakina in the Wimbledon third round. It's the third time in her career that she's scored multiple Top 5 wins in a single season -- in 2018, the Belgian defeated Elina Svitolina at the Australian Open and Sloane Stephens in Cincinnati; in 2021, she topped Svitolina again at the Gippsland Trophy in Melbourne, and Simona Halep in Madrid.

Mertens advances to her second quarterfinal at WTA 1000 level or above this year, following her run to the last eight of Wimbledon. She'll take on another former winner, 2023 champion and No. 8 seed Iga Swiatek -- another player she has yet to defeat, though her 0-2 record against the Pole may seem less intimidating after finally getting over the Gauff hurdle. Mertens will be bidding to reach her first semifinal at WTA 1000 level or above since Dubai 2021.

content.title: By the numbers: Swiatek defeats Jovic to strengthen WTA 1000 record
content.description: Iga Swiatek defeated American teenager Iva Jovic 6-1, 6-3 to reach the quarterfinals of the China Open in Beijing. The win moved Swiatek level with Serena Williams on 148 WTA 1000 main-draw victories and into her 31st quarterfinal at the level.

related.label: 'I was shaking!' Muchova edges Osaka on ninth match point in Beijing thriller
Bartunkova’s year of growth continues to pay off with a semifinal run in Beijing
São Paulo makes history with South America's first-ever WTA Coaches Workshop

content.body:
In the first career meeting between six-time Grand Slam champion Iga Swiatek of Poland and rising American teenager Iva Jovic, Swiatek advanced to the quarterfinals of the China Open in Beijing with a 6-1, 6-3 victory Wednesday.

Swiatek dominated the opening set, winning the first five games and earning two set points in the sixth game before Jovic held serve to get on the scoreboard. The Pole then held serve to close out the set on her fifth set point.

The second set began with Swiatek breaking early to take a 2-0 lead, but Jovic began finding more range and depth on her groundstrokes. The 18-year-old, ranked a career-high No. 13 in the world, broke back to level the set.

Jovic, who entered the match on a six-match winning streak after winning the Guadalajara title last month, saved two more break points in the next game to take a 3-2 lead. But Swiatek broke twice in a row to complete the victory in 1 hour, 36 minutes.

"For sure (today), I was using more of the chances that I got," Swiatek told the media after the win. "I was more proactive. Maybe changing the directions more instead of just being solid, more intense. When I needed that, I could play long rallies and be in defense, as well. Everything was working today."

Iga advances ✅ @iga_swiatek caps off an incredible showing in Beijing against Jovic! #ChinaOpen https://t.co/jsTcgEmr8y

— wta (@WTA) October 7, 2026

Here are some of the notable numbers from Swiatek's fourth-round win:

9: Swiatek now has nine wins against players ranked in the top 20 on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz in 2026, against eight losses. She also recorded her 35th win against a player outside the top 10 this season, against eight losses.

31: Swiatek is through to her 31st career WTA 1000 quarterfinal. Among active players, only world No. 2 Aryna Sabalenka has reached more, with 33.

36: Swiatek has 36 wins against top-15 opponents at WTA 1000 events. Among active players, only Serena Williams, with 44, and Sabalenka, with 41, have more.

126: Swiatek has now won 126 of 128 WTA 1000 matches in which she won the first set. Both those losses have come in 2026 - to Maria Sakkari in Doha and to Magda Linette in Miami.

148: The victory was Swiatek's 148th WTA 1000 main-draw win, moving her level with Serena Williams. Among active players, only Sabalenka, with 156, has more. Overall, Swiatek and Williams are tied for seventh place for most wins since the WTA 1000 format was introduced in 2009.

Swiatek will face No. 13 seed Elise Mertens in the quarterfinals. Mertens, who defeated No. 3 seed Coco Gauff 6-3, 6-3 in another fourth-round clash on Tuesday, has not beaten Swiatek in their two previous meetings.

"I feel like my game has improved," Swiatek said reflecting on her recent form. "Obviously sometimes playing the tournament is a bit tricky. Not everything is depending on you. I believe what I'm doing makes sense moving forward.

"That gives me the most confidence. For sure when you have great results on a match, it's always a good boost of confidence. But tennis is tough. You need to be ready for every match. Your previous results are not going to give you anything. I'm going to push no matter what and we'll see how it goes."

content.title: Alexandra Eala steps out in Chanel at Paris Fashion Week
content.description: Alexandra Eala continues to make the fashion show rounds, this time appearing at the Chanel Spring/Summer 2027 show, part of Paris Fashion Week.

related.label: Week in review: Top seeds fall and a barrage of breakthroughs in Beijing
'I was shaking!' Muchova edges Osaka on ninth match point in Beijing thriller

content.body:
Alexandra Eala's star, and influence, continues to rise off the court, on all corners of the globe.

The most recent example was this week in France, where Eala attended the Chanel Spring/Summer 2027 show, part of Paris Fashion Week.

Eala, who won her first WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz title in Washington, D.C. this past summer, stepped out in a Chanel tweed jacket over a black shirt. Dark pants complemented the fit.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Alexandra Eala (@alex.eala)

"It's so surreal to experience the collection, to experience Chanel in Paris," Eala told Vogue Philippines. "I wouldn't have had it any other way for my first show."

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Vogue Philippines (@voguephilippines)

Eala's Paris Fashion Week debut comes a little under a month after appearing in several shows during New York Fashion Week. After the US Open, she attended the Tory Burch Spring/Summer 2027 showcase, where she mingled with actress Amanda Seyfried, singer Lauryn Hill and former Vogue editor-in-chief Anna Wintour. 

Eala was also spotted in the front row at Michael Kors' Spring/Summer 2027 soiree, held at The Museum of Modern Art's Sculpture Garden, and closed out her Fashion Week festivities at Calvin Klein's exhibition.

"I love the twin dresses," the World No. 18 told Vogue of her favorite Chanel looks in Paris. "Very flowy. I feel like one was inspired by day, and the other by night. I also love the very structured dresses, very simple. So many details.

"I love how they blended simple silhouettes, details, and I think everything was very wearable. That's what stood out to me."

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Vogue Philippines (@voguephilippines)

Eala's start to the Asian Swing didn't go as planned, losing to then-World No. 180 Tatiana Prozorova in her opening match in Singapore. Eala let a lead slip away in the 4-6, 7-5, 6-3 defeat, in a match that went over three hours.

She'll look to rebound next week in Wuhan, the final WTA 1000 tournament of the season. She's lost her opening matches in her two previous Wuhan appearances, first to Katerina Siniakova in 2024 and then to Moyuka Uchijima last year. This will be her first time playing the tournament as a direct entrant.

content.title: Breaking down the unlikely quarterfinal matchups in Beijing
content.description: Zheng Qinwen plays Elina Svitolina, Elise Mertens takes on Iga Swiatek, Ekaterina Alexandrova faces Mirra Andreeva and Karolina Muchova squares off with Nikola Bartunkova in the China Open quarterfinals. We break all the matches down.

related.label: Zheng powers into Beijing last eight with three-set win over Charaeva
Mertens beats Gauff for first time in six meetings to make Beijing quarters
By the numbers: Swiatek defeats Jovic to strengthen WTA 1000 record

content.body:
At the season’s most recent Grand Slam, the US Open, the top five seeds reached the quarterfinals. The top four advanced to the semifinals, with the No. 1 and No. 2 seeds meeting for the title.

Beijing has gone in the other direction. At the second-to-last 1000-level event of the season on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz, the top two seeds are already out, and only one of the top five remains with the quarterfinals set.

Among the final eight is an unseeded home favorite, a pair of Grand Slam champions, several tried-and-true veterans and an up-and-comer having the best tournament of her career.

Here's what you need to know about the matchups ahead of the China Open quarterfinals.

Zheng Qinwen vs. [6] Elina Svitolina

First meeting

Zheng is becoming awfully familiar with three-set matches. She won four straight three-setters to reach the US Open quarterfinals, then lost another three-set match there.

The pattern has continued at her home tournament in Beijing, where all four of her matches have gone the distance. The unseeded World No. 54 has come back from a set down twice and upset No. 15 seed Anna Kalinskaya and No. 18 seed Marie Bouzkova. On Wednesday, she defeated Alina Charaeva 6-1, 2-6, 6-4.

It's been a smoother, and less physically demanding, tournament for Elina Svitolina. The sixth seed has played one fewer match after receiving a first-round bye, and has won six consecutive sets with ease after dropping her first to Katerina Siniakova last week.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by WTA (@wta)

Surprisingly, despite both players being veterans with a track record of success, this will be their first career meeting. Zheng will surely be buoyed by her home crowd as she looks to make her first semifinal since June 2025, at Queen's Club. Svitolina most recently made the semis in Toronto, in August, and is in pursuit of her third title of the year.

[13] Elise Mertens vs. [8] Iga Swiatek

Swiatek leads the head-to-head 2-0

Elise Mertens has had to work for her quarterfinal berth. Her first-round match against Katie Volynets was a doozy. Mertens was in total control, leading 6-0, 3-0, with four opportunities to take a 4-0 lead in that second set.

But before she could comprehend what went wrong, she found herself down a break in the third. She rallied to win that match 6-0, 4-6, 7-5 in just under three hours. The World No. 19 bore down late in her next match as well, coming from 2-0 down in the decider to beat Jelena Ostapenko.

Surprisingly, her most comfortable win of the tournament came on Wednesday against Coco Gauff, whom she had never beaten in five tries. Mertens closed the match out strong, winning 10 of her last 11 service points and closing out the 6-3, 6-3 win with an ace.

Iga Swiatek had a close call in her second match, somehow finding a way to beat Donna Vekic after trailing 6-4, 5-2. But her fourth-round match against Iva Jovic was never in doubt, an authoritative 6-1, 6-3 win in which "everything was working," as Swiatek accurately put it.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by WTA (@wta)

Swiatek has never dropped a set to Mertens. In their lone match on hard courts, in Miami last year, Swiatek beat Mertens 7-6 (2), 6-1.

[19] Ekaterina Alexandrova vs. [4] Mirra Andreeva

Alexandrova leads the head-to-head 2-0

Ekaterina Alexandrova has pulled off a couple of big upsets in Beijing, coming from a set down against 11th seed Diana Shnaider and following that up with a commanding win over fifth-seeded Linda Noskova. Alexandrova wasn't broken against the Wimbledon champion, dropping just four games in a little over an hour.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by WTA (@wta)

She'll face a well-rested and in-form Andreeva, who lost her first set in Beijing to Yuan Yue. It's been smooth sailing since then, though. She rallied to win the next 12 games for the three-set win, the rare double bagel on the back end, then breezed past unseeded Polina Kudermetova and Daria Snigur to book her spot in the quarterfinals.

After the 6-2, 6-2 win over Snigur, Andreeva took to the practice courts -- not her choice, she clarified -- to work on returns. She'll certainly need a strong return game against Alexandrova, who hit six aces and won 88 percent of her first-serve points against Noskova.

Andreeva will be the favorite, considering her higher ranking and more recent success, but Alexandrova comes in with the confidence of a 2-0 head-to-head advantage. This will be their first meeting on hard courts, though. Alexandrova beat Andreeva in straight sets on clay last year, and beat her again on grass, in Bad Homburg, back in June. 

[7] Karolina Muchova vs. [26] Nikola Bartunkova 

First meeting

What a fun encounter this should be between two wildly talented Czechs, one an established veteran and the other a rising up-and-comer.

Karolina Muchova and Nikola Bartunkova have both taken dramatic paths to the Beijing quarterfinals. After Muchova beat Katie Boulter in straight sets, she came from a set down to knock off Liudmila Samsonova.

But that was just an appetizer for her next match, a nearly-three-hour marathon against Naomi Osaka that came down to a third-set tiebreak. Muchova was down breaks in both the first and third sets, and eventually clinched the match on her ninth match point. Her much-improved backhand let her down late in the third set, but she stayed aggressive with it, firing a backhand winner down the line to set up the ninth match point.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by WTA (@wta)

As for Bartunkova, she's fresh off the biggest win of her career, a 6-4, 6-3 upset of second-seeded Aryna Sabalenka. She then avoided the post-upset hangover, beating Sinja Kraus 6-0, 4-6, 6-3 to book a spot in a WTA 1000 quarterfinal for the first time.

Despite their 10-year age gap, and having never played on tour, they know each others' games well. They train at the same club in Prague and are frequent practice partners. Expect plenty of finesse, touch and exceptional shot-making in this one.

content.title: Bartunkova’s year of growth continues to pay off with a semifinal run in Beijing
content.description: Nikola Bartunkova will play in her first WTA 1000 semifinal in Beijing, and is in the middle of another run that's transcended her into the top 35 over the past year.

related.label: By the numbers: Bartunkova stuns Sabalenka to reach Beijing last 16
'I was shaking!' Muchova edges Osaka on ninth match point in Beijing thriller
On verge of first WTA 1000 quarterfinal, get to know No. 118 Alina Charaeva

content.body:
Editor’s note: At the Internazionali BNL d’Italia in Rome, wtatennis.com sat down with Nikola Bartunkova in a get-to-know interview about her game-style, rise through the ranks and more.

BEIJING -- A year and a half ago, Nikola Bartunkova was ranked No. 517 in the world and playing weekly World Tennis/ITF Events in Europe. 

Eighteen months later, she’s transcended through the rankings and sits at career-high No. 34 ahead of her first WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz 1000 semifinal at the China Open, a run highlighted by her upset of World No. 2 Aryna Sabalenka in the third round. Tuesday, she defeated Sinja Kraus 6-0, 4-6, 6-3 in the Round of 16, and Thursday, she upset No. 7 seed Karolina Muchova 6-3, 6-0 in the quarterfinal. 

“It’s been an unbelievable year for me,” Bartunkova said in Beijing. “I didn’t expect before this year that I play like this and I will be here. It’s great, but just now I focus on myself, improve my game because it’s still 50-50 every match. 

“I’m still young, so I need to have more experience and this is my goal now.”

For Bartunkova, it wasn’t just one tournament that really elevated her ranking. Rather, it was the 20-year-old’s consistency from tournament-to-tournament that gradually put her in the spotlight. 

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by WTA (@wta)

Bartunkova’s first breakout came in Guadalajara last September. As a main-draw wild card, she cruised through to the semifinals, where eventual champion and current top 15 player Iva Jovic edged her out. 

Then, at the turn of the season, Bartunkova really caught tennis fans’ attention at the Australian Open in Melbourne, where she was a qualifier. 

Advancing to her first Grand Slam main draw, she upset Daria Kasatkina in the first round and then produced the tournament’s first top 10 upset in a victory over Belinda Bencic in the second round. Bencic had entered the match on a 12-match singles winning streak.

On the clay as a lucky loser in Rome, she produced a run to the Round of 16, upsetting Madison Keys in the third round. During the grass-court season, she made the final at the Birmingham 125 before narrowly losing to then-No. 1 Sabalenka in Berlin’s quarterfinals, a match she proved to herself she could compete with the best. 

Therefore, it wasn’t a surprise to her that she ousted Sabalenka in Beijing. 

“It tells that I beat a No. 1 player, and she’s a Grand Slam champion,” Bartunkova said. “In Berlin, I had a very close match with her.  I knew can play with [top players]. 

“From Berlin, I knew I could do this."

This meteoric rise can come down to the Czech’s brand of tennis, one she dubs as “unpredictable.” It’s an aggressive style of tennis, one with plenty of shot variety, and she took inspiration from Roger Federer and Carlos Alcaraz, Bartunkova said after beating Bencic in Melbourne. 

"I think my game is the same with all the players," Bartunkova said on her mixture of forehands, slices and volleys. "Sometimes [the opponent] has better movement, more faster, but my game is the same always. I try to go for volleys. I try to go more for my shots, so that's the plan."

This playstyle is what’s powered her through Beijing, and she’ll put it to the test against either Mirra Andreeva or Ekaterina Alexandrova in the final four.
content.author: Cole Bambini
content.summary: Nikola Bartunkova will play in her first WTA 1000 semifinal in Beijing, and is in the middle of another run that's transcended her into the top 35 over the past year.

content.title: 'I was shaking!' Muchova edges Osaka on ninth match point in Beijing thriller
content.description: Karolina Muchova came from a break down in both the first and third sets, then needed nine match points to get over the line against Naomi Osaka in the China Open fourth round.

related.label: Andreeva seeks first win over Alexandrova in Beijing quarterfinal
On verge of first WTA 1000 quarterfinal, get to know No. 118 Alina Charaeva
What's it like being a ball kid at the China Open? Here's what they said

content.body:
No. 7 seed Karolina Muchova came through a spectacular fourth-round tilt at the China Open on Tuesday, denying No. 12 seed Naomi Osaka from a break down in both the first and third sets and eventually sealing her ninth match point to advance 7-5, 1-6, 7-6(7) in 2 hours and 52 minutes.

Muchova, who trailed 4-1 in the opener and 3-1 in the decider, held triple-match point at 5-4 in the third set on Osaka's serve -- but was unable to take a total of five opportunities to seal victory in that game. In the ensuing tiebreak, the Czech player missed another three match points, but converted the ninth in style with a delicate backhand volley winner.

"I honestly didn't even believe I will finish the match," Muchova said in her on-court interview. "So many match points, I didn't know how many. After a match point I was like, 'OK, I'm going for it,' but then I think she always played great and steady, and didn't make mistakes -- unlike me, unfortunately! I was shaking. I'm happy that I made the last volley and it was really so close. Naomi could be standing here. It's me, and I'm really grateful for it."

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by WTA (@wta)

In the eighth edition of the pair's six-year rivalry, Muchova backed up two grass-court victories this year to improve to 5-3 overall against Osaka -- though she still trails 3-2 on outdoor hard courts. She booked her place in her fourth quarterfinal at WTA 1000 level or above this season, following her Doha title, Wimbledon final run and Miami semifinal showing. 

Here are the key takeaways from Muchova's win:

Her backhand nearly lost her the match ... but ultimately won it for her

In previous seasons, Muchova's drive backhand has been an area of vulnerability for her -- both more prone to breaking down and less lethal than her forehand wing. She's levelled up on that side in 2026, one of the reasons this has been the most consistent of her career to date.

But as she tried to close Osaka out, it nearly let her down again. She squandered three of the five match points she held at 5-4 with backhand unforced errors -- Osaka saved the other two with an ace and a service winner. Another backhand sprayed wide enabled Osaka to hold that game, and another dumped in the net wasted her seventh match point. (Match points six and eight were lost on forehand unforced errors.)

No wonder that, at 7-7 in the tiebreak, Osaka began targeting that wing exclusively -- and nor did the 2019 champion hold back as she pummelled it at full force. Muchova managed to withstand all the pace, though -- and then find the space she needed to redirect it for a winner down the line to bring up her ninth and final match point.

"I think I was solid from the backhand side today," Muchova said. "I feel like all the players are hitting to my backhand side. But I'd say it was a shot that won the match for me today."

Muchova remains perfect in third-set tiebreaks this year

The result extended Muchova's record in third-set tiebreaks this year to a perfect 3-0 -- she also edged Ajla Tomljanovic 4-6, 6-1, 7-6(5) in the Brisbane second round, her first match of the season, and then saved a match point to deny Coco Gauff 6-2, 1-6, 7-6[10] in the Wimbledon semifinals.

The only other player with a 3-0 record in deciding tiebreaks this year is Rabat champion Petra Marcinko (who won her trio against Camila Osorio in Auckland, Yelyzaveta Kotliar in Rabat and Antonia Ruzic in Eastbourne). No player has won more than three deciding tiebreaks at tour level this year; Anna Kalinskaya has also won three, but has lost two as well.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by WTA (@wta)

Muchova's strong third-set tiebreak performance isn't new -- the 30-year-old owns an 8-3 career record in them at tour level, dating back to 2019. She hasn't lost a third-set tiebreak since the second round of the 2023 Australian Open, when she fell 6-7(1), 6-2, 7-6[6] to Danielle Collins.

That's a contrast to Osaka's 2-6 career record in deciding tiebreaks. The four-time major champion has not won one since the 2019 Stuttgart quarterfinals, when she edged Donna Vekic 6-3, 4-6, 7-6(4).

In this one, Muchova acknowledged that she "got a bit lucky" -- at 6-6, Osaka hammered a forehand return crosscourt as she sought to reach match point for the first time. Muchova only just got her racquet on the ball in response -- and her forehand dribbled over the net cord for a fortuitous steal.

Muchova faces a crafty Czech in her own mold next

Next up for Muchova is an all-Czech derby against No. 26 seed Nikola Bartunkova, who backed up her third-round upset of Aryna Sabalenka with a 6-0, 4-6, 6-3 defeat of Sinja Kraus to make her first WTA 1000 quarterfinal. It'll be the first time the pair have played each other, and an intriguing matchup. The 20-year-old Bartunkova's potent blend of power and finesse has drawn plenty of comparisons with Muchova as she's risen from No. 126 at the start of the year to her current career high of No. 34.

Muchova has been aware of Bartunkova's talent for a while longer. They both train at the same club in Prague, and are frequent practise partners on tour.

"I'm not surprised it could be a Czech match," she said. "It's on every tournament, in all the rounds you can play a Czech player. It's not really surprising anymore, I would say ... I never played Niki. She is a crafty player."

content.title: Andreeva seeks first win over Alexandrova in Beijing quarterfinal
content.description: Mirra Andreeva and Ekaterina Alexandrova advanced to the China Open quarterfinals with identical 6-2, 6-2 victories in Beijing on Tuesday. The fourth-seeded Andreeva will bid for her first win over No. 19 seed Alexandrova, who has won both of their previous meetings.

related.label: Gauff pulls away late to defeat 16-year-old Sun in Beijing
Zheng holds off Bouzkova in third straight three-setter in Beijing
Swiatek rallies from 6-4, 5-2 down to beat Vekic and reach Beijing last 16

content.body:
No. 4 seed Mirra Andreeva will take on No. 19 seed Ekaterina Alexandrova in the quarterfinals of the China Open in Beijing after both players scored comfortable straight-set victories Tuesday.

Andreeva was the first to take to Centre Court in Beijing against unseeded Daria Snigur, who was playing her first round-of-16 match at a WTA 1000 event. Andreeva dropped serve only once in the 1-hour, 3-minute contest while breaking her opponent five times in her 6-2, 6-2 win.

Closes it out and advances 🔥 Mirra Andreeva defeats Snigur in straight sets to reach the quarterfinals in Beijing! #ChinaOpen https://t.co/kkrF6vgaV8

— wta (@WTA) October 6, 2026

Andreeva hit 18 winners on the day against just 15 unforced errors, while Snigur had 32 unforced errors to 17 winners.

The 19-year-old is through to the quarterfinals in Beijing for the second time in her career. She lost to Zheng Qinwen in her only other quarterfinal here in 2024. She also advances to the last eight for the 11th time on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercdes-Benz this year.

It also marked Andreeva's 48th win of the season on tour, her most in any season so far. She trails only Jessica Pegula (50) and Elena Rybakina (49) in match wins this year.

Andreeva happy with performance but heads to practice later

"I think today I was serving well," Andreeva said after the win. "I also think that I was defending well also because she's a very aggressive player. I thought being a good defender today would be good and useful. I think I did these two things the best today."

While Andreeva, who hit six aces in the match, was happy with her performance, she was back on the practice courts after the match - something which she said was her team's decision.

"Just so you know, it was not my idea. It was not up to me (smiling)," she told the media. "It's the second day in a row the team kind of caught me off guard. Conchita (her coach) told me, We have practice court eight. I'm like, Yeah, great, exciting. We just did a lot of returns because I'm going to play against the big servers, big hitters. We just did a lot of returns. I did a lot of just basic stuff to kind of clean and feel good after the match, clean my shots."

Alexandrova becomes oldest first-time quarterfinalist in Beijing

Right after Andreeva made it into the last eight, No. 19 seed Alexandrova and No. 5 seed Linda Noskova, who reached the final here last year, followed on Centre Court. Alexandrova was equally dominant, winning 6-2, 6-2 without dropping serve in the 1-hour, 6-minute contest.

Aces it out ✅ Ekaterina Alexandrova defeats Wimbledon champion Noskova in straight sets after an incredible performance! #ChinaOpen https://t.co/DhyUR7PToS

— wta (@WTA) October 6, 2026

Alexandrova is through to the last eight in Beijing for the first time in her career. At 31, she becomes the oldest player to reach her maiden quarterfinal at the China Open in the tournament's history. She also becomes the third-oldest player to reach the last eight in Beijing, after Serena Williams and Shuai Zhang.

The win puts her into her seventh WTA 1000 quarterfinal of her career and the second of the season, after Toronto. It also marks her 22nd career win over a Top 10 player, her third of the season.

"Today's match, it wasn't easy because I know Linda, she plays so well, especially this season," Alexandrova said after the match. "I knew it's going to be difficult. With the sun today at the start, it wasn't easy because it was difficult to see the ball. I think it was a pretty good match for me. Good serve, good shots. I'm overall kind of happy with the performance and I'm glad that I could finish in two sets. Just be in the quarterfinal here in Beijing, I think it's a great start for the whole Asia Swing."

Alexandrova leads Andreeva 2-0 in head-to-head

Alexandrova has played Andreeva twice before and come away the winner each time - defeating the French Open champion at Stuttgart in 2025 and Bad Homburg in 2026 - a stat that Andreeva is well aware of.

"Well, one thing I do know for sure, I didn't beat her yet (smiling)," Andreeva said, looking ahead to her next opponent. "I will try my best with Conchita to see how I play against her, what to change, try something new that I can try to bring into the match. For sure it's going to be a great, entertaining match. She's a great player. I don't know. Pretty excited to finally get that first win against her."

Meanwhile, Alexandrova prefers not to think about their head-to-head.

"I'm trying not to think about the head-to-head," she said. "When you thinking about that, it's create more tension and more pressure on yourself. It's going to be difficult, for sure. If you put even more pressure on yourself, it's probably won't help you. We played a couple times. Every match you would play, it's different. Every time is a different condition. You can have two matches before and third will be completely different than that. It's a nice statistic, but it's better not to think about it."
content.summary: Mirra Andreeva and Ekaterina Alexandrova advanced to the China Open quarterfinals with identical 6-2, 6-2 victories in Beijing on Tuesday. The fourth-seeded Andreeva will bid for her first win over No. 19 seed Alexandrova, who has won both of their previous meetings.

content.title: On verge of first WTA 1000 quarterfinal, get to know No. 118 Alina Charaeva
content.description: World No. 118 Alina Charaeva is in the middle of her best season to date, and ahead of her fourth-round showdown with Zheng Qinwen, get to know the 24-year-old from Armenia.

related.label: Charaeva upsets new World No. 1 Rybakina in Beijing second round
Gauff pulls away late to defeat 16-year-old Sun in Beijing
Zheng pays tribute to Chinese cartoon after beating Bouzkova

content.body:
BEIJING -- World No. 118 Alina Charaeva put herself on the map with an upset -- a second-round comeback win in Beijing over new World No. 1 Elena Rybakina, who was playing her first match since the US Open. 

On Monday, she defeated Sonay Kartal in a much smoother 6-4, 6-1 win to advance to the China Open fourth round and is on the verge of a spot in her first WTA 1000 quarterfinal, but will have to get through fan-favorite Chinese wild card Zheng Qinwen on Wednesday. 

"It feels pretty special because it's my first time [in a WTA 1000 fourth round] and actually the first time in Beijing as well," Charaeva said. "I'm just really happy with my work and how I've managed my emotions and mental part as well."

Following her third-round win Monday, Charaeva sat down briefly with wtatennis.com in Beijing. Get to know the 24-year-old representing Armenia:

She's been with her coach for eight years

Charaeva's coach Carlos Martinez, and they have been working today for the last eight years. Martinez owns CMC Competition, a training tennis academy near Barcelona, Spain, where Charaeva resides. 

Martinez has brought tons of experience to Charaeva, having worked with notable player Daria Kasatkina, Simona Halep, Svetlana Kuznetsova and more. 

"He's actually like my father," Charaeva joked on how long she's worked with him. "'I'm really happy we achieved this moment together because this is our dream, and he's a really nice coach."

Charaeva has never played in a Grand Slam main draw

Charaeva has played qualifiers at each of the four majors at least once, but has never advanced out of the qualifying draw.

The closest she's come was falling short in the third round of qualifying at Wimbledon a few months ago and the 2025 US Open.

Should she continue winning in Beijing and end the season on a strong note, Charaeva could find herself with a strong enough ranking to earn direct entry into the Australian Open. Currently, she's projected to surpass her career high rank of No. 108, which she obtained ahead of the US Open.

During the Asian Swing last season, Charaeva advanced to the semifinal and final of two WTA 125 events in China and was eliminated in the first round in Tokyo and Chennai.

It's been a busy season

At the beginning of the season, Charaeva was sitting just outside of the top 160.

Now, with main draw 2026 appearances in Beijing, Rouen, Madrid, Iasi, Hamburg, Cincinnati, São Paulo and Seoul in addition to a 125 title in Midland and other strong finishes at that level, Charaeva is the middle of her best season to date. 

"Of course, people say this season is when you make a big step, but I feel it was not kind of like one big step," Charaeva said. "It was a lot of years of hard work for this result. This year and last year, I was much consistent. I didn't have a lot of injuries, so that's pretty great."

Her upcoming match against Zheng will be her 60th of the season with plenty more to go -- she has a 36-23 record on the season, including notable wins over Sofia Kenin in Seoul last week, Sara Bejlek at the Birmingham 125 and Nikola Bartunkova at Madrid qualifying. 

"This season I started to compete in a higher level, compete with a better players," Charaeva added. "For me and for my coach, our mentality is when I start to compete with better players -- even if I lose or win -- this is where you get the real level of tennis.

"I'm competing, maybe losing so much [sometimes], but we're really tight with really top players. That's where I build my level and I'm really happy that it's finally paying off."

The history she's made thus far

In her win over Rybakina, Charaeva made some unique history:

Representing Armenia, she became the first Armenian player to defeat a World No. 1 since the first WTA rankings in 1975. 

Charaeva is now the second player to defeat a World No. 1 in that top player's first match holding that ranking, joining Kristina Mladenovic in Dubai 2019 -- Mladenovic defeated Naomi Osaka. 

Since the debut of the rankings in 1975, she's the lowest-ranked player to complete a comeback win over a World No. 1. 

Since 1990, Charaeva is just the third player to defeat the World No. 1 in their first match against a WTA top 10 opponent (Julie Coin, US Open 2008 and Chang Kai-Chen, Tokyo 2009).

*Stats courtesy of OptaFacts
